confirmed.title: Auto-fetch trusts the peer-declared attachment size; the real blob size is never checked or capped
confirmed.scenario: Any member of a shared server (or a DM contact) posts a message whose Attachment says size=1000 while its hash is the hash of a 50 GB blob they serve. validate_message (tincan-core state.rs:818) never bounds Attachment.size, and auto_fetch (transfers.rs:266-270) compares only the declared a.size against autoFetchLimit (25 MiB by default). So every online member queues FetchReq::Auto, and start_download (transfers.rs:244-248) calls files.download with no size limit (tincan-files download.rs has no cap). The true size shows up in TransferInfo.total after the first verified chunk (download.rs:301-309), but on_transfer (transfers.rs:287-318) only forwards it to the UI. Each victim downloads the whole 50 GB unattended until the disk fills, and also holds one of the 3 download slots (files.rs:50) for the whole time, which stalls every other attachment. Each victim then re-serves the blob. Clip pulls already defend against this (media/clips.rs:450-452 cancels anything over 5 MiB); attachments do not.
confirmed.fix: Robust fix: give Files::download a size cap (per call or per kind) and fail the request inside attempt() as soon as bf.size() is known (download.rs:303-309), dropping its tag. This does not depend on FileEvents arriving. Minimal app-side fix: in on_transfer, for BlobKind::Attachment, when info.total > MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES call files.cancel(hash) and spawn files.remove_kind(hash, BlobKind::Attachment), as clips.rs:452-456 does. remove_kind rather than remove, so a clip tag is not dropped. Then set the download record to failed, emit transfer-updated as failed, and remember the hash as rejected in kv so Auto, Resume and cmd_download refuse it. Do not cancel on a mismatch with the indexed AttRef.size: that index is first-writer-wins (APP-CORE-06), so a peer could use a mismatch to block a legitimate file. Also skip auto_fetch and cmd_download when the declared a.size > MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES, and apply the same cap to the Resume path that has no origin (transfers.rs:147).
confirmed.verify: Confirmed end to end. validate_message (tincan-core state.rs:818-837) checks only the name and mime lengths, never Attachment.size. auto_fetch compares only the declared a.size (transfers.rs:267). start_download calls files.download with no cap (transfers.rs:248, download.rs:134-177). attempt() learns the real size at download.rs:303-309 but never checks it. on_transfer (transfers.rs:287-318) only forwards it to the UI. finish() then emits Completed, and the pump calls have_add (pump.rs:330-333), so every victim re-serves the blob. cmd_download (transfers.rs:348-358) and the Resume path (130-148) are uncapped too. Each oversized download holds one of the 3 slots (files.rs:50) while it runs. After a disk-full LocalError the tag stays, so partial_downloads resumes it on the next start. The attacker only needs a large (even sparse, all-zero) file to serve. Legit clients cannot produce such an attachment, because import_attachments refuses anything over MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES (transfers.rs:447).

confirmed.title: open_file shell-executes peer-named files; the name sanitizer can turn '.pdf' into '.exe' and keeps RTLO
confirmed.scenario: cmd_open_file (transfers.rs:397,412) exports the blob as safe_file_name(<peer-supplied name>) and runs `explorer.exe <path>`, which runs .exe/.js/.bat/.lnk/.hta files directly. The file gets no Mark-of-the-Web, so SmartScreen and WSH never warn. safe_file_name truncates from the front with `out.chars().take(200)` (shell.rs:101), but core allows names up to 255 chars (MAX_ATTACHMENT_NAME_CHARS). A peer sends name = "invoice" + 189 spaces + ".exe.pdf" (204 chars) with mime application/pdf. The UI shows a PDF icon and a name ending in .exe.pdf, but the exported file is "invoice<spaces>.exe", and clicking Open runs the attacker's PE. Separately, shell.rs:88 drops only Cc controls (char::is_control), so U+202E survives: "photo‮gnp.exe" displays as "photoexe.png" and exports as an .exe. The image path (Attachment.tsx:115) has the same problem: clicking the preview of a file declared image/gif and named x.js, built as a GIF/JS polyglot that renders, launches WScript.
confirmed.fix: In cmd_open_file, use an allowlist rather than a denylist. Shell-open only known-safe extensions (raster images, audio, video, pdf, txt). For everything else, and for an image/* attachment whose extension does not match the sniffed type, run `explorer.exe /select,<path>` to reveal the file instead. Run this check on the final path, including the previous_export branch (transfers.rs:389-390), which reuses a stored path. For image-preview clicks, export with the sniffed type's extension. In safe_file_name, drop Unicode format characters (U+200E/F, U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069, U+061C, U+FEFF), truncate the stem so the last extension is kept, and trim trailing dots and spaces again after truncating. After export, write a `:Zone.Identifier` stream with ZoneId=3, so SmartScreen, Office Protected View and macro blocking apply.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. safe_file_name truncates to 200 chars after the extension (shell.rs:101), so "invoice" + 189 spaces + ".exe.pdf" exports as "invoice<spaces>.exe". HTML collapses the spaces, so the card shows "invoice .exe.pdf" with a PDF icon (Attachment.tsx:16,141-143). char::is_control matches only Cc, so U+202E survives (shell.rs:88). cmd_open_file passes the UI-supplied peer name (Attachment.tsx:69,115) to explorer.exe (shell.rs:133), which runs .exe/.js/.hta. files.export writes no Mark-of-the-Web. The image path is the worst: the preview never shows the name (Attachment.tsx:110-118). serve_mime sniffs GIF/PNG magic bytes, so a polyglot renders (shell.rs:49-57). One click on what looks like a picture named x.js or x.hta (any image with an HTA payload appended) launches WScript or mshta.

confirmed.title: Every held blob is announced to every server host and DM peer, and any member or contact may fetch any of them
confirmed.scenario: At start the app announces every complete blob from all conversations, private DMs included, with net.set_have(files.complete_hashes()) (app.rs:178). The pump calls have_add for every completed attachment whatever its conversation (pump.rs:330-333). net puts that one global list in each server Hello and Have to the host (net.rs:324), and broadcast_have sends deltas to every DM link (dm.rs:244-251). The AccessPolicy the app installs (app.rs:156-158, update_policy app.rs:269-282, on_dm_opened commands.rs:293) is a per-peer union: every member of any server plus every DM peer, including strangers whose incoming DM created a DmOpened. tincan-files checks it once per connection and then serves any hash (provider.rs:31-38, get: RequestMode::None). Example: Mallory hosts server S, which Alice is in (hosting is not a privilege). Alice's Hello to Mallory lists hash H of a photo Bob sent Alice in a DM. Mallory dials Alice on /iroh-bytes/4, the policy allows him because he is a member of S, and he downloads Bob's private photo. Any stranger who DMs Alice also gets later Have deltas and the same access.
confirmed.fix: Authorize per (peer, hash) in tincan-files: set get and get_many (and observe) to RequestMode::Intercept and change the policy to allow(peer, hash). The app needs a persistent hash -> set-of-conversations table, written whenever an attachment is indexed, sent or downloaded. The current atts map cannot authorize: it is filled lazily, holds one conversation per hash, is cleared at 50k, and app/att keeps one conversation that each download overwrites. Allow a request if the peer is a current member of one of those servers or the DM peer of one of those DMs. Allow clip hashes to members of any shared server. Per-conversation Have and DmHello lists need a tincan-net API change (set_have per conversation), so they are not an app-only step. Interim app-only step: leave hashes whose only origin is a DM out of set_have and have_add. DM who_has always returns the contact (notes-tincan-net.md:32), so DM downloads do not need the announcement. This does not stop cross-server leaks.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed, and worse than stated. The app feeds every held hash, DM ones included, into one global list (app.rs:178, pump.rs:330-333). The policy is a per-peer union (app.rs:156-158,269-282, commands.rs:293). provider.rs:31-38 checks access once per connection (connected: Intercept, get: None) and then serves any hash. Besides the Hello to each server host, dm.rs:450 answers every incoming DM dial with dm_hello, which carries the full have_list (dm.rs:431). Incoming DMs from strangers are accepted (notes-tincan-net.md:35), and on_dm_opened adds the dialer to the allow set. So anyone who knows my user id, which every server-mate sees in the member list, can open a DM without my consent, receive the full hash list at once, and download any blob. That includes other contacts' DM attachments and attachments from servers the attacker is not in.

confirmed.title: FileEvent lag is only logged: lost Completed and Transfer events are never recovered
confirmed.scenario: The files broadcast holds 512 events (files.rs:54), and its docs say a lagged receiver must re-query (files.rs:499-500). The pump's `biased` select polls net_rx before file_rx (pump.rs:97-119), so during a large history sync (net events streaming in, the fetch worker issuing up to 1024 auto-fetch downloads, each emitting Queued, Downloading, progress every 250 ms, Complete and Completed) file_rx can fall more than 512 behind. On Lagged the app only logs at debug level (pump.rs:121). A lost FileEvent::Completed means net.have_add(hash) never runs, so this member is never announced as a holder until the next restart. Once the uploader goes offline, others' who_has finds nobody, which defeats "attachments keep downloading when the uploader is offline". A lost final Transfer leaves the UI on downloading/queued for good, and a lost Completed{Clip} means a pulled clip never enters the library.
confirmed.fix: On RecvError::Lagged from file_rx: call core.net.set_have(core.files.complete_hashes()). For every hash in transfer_states, and every hash with a download record still queued or downloading, re-run on_transfer with files.transfer(hash). For held hashes this yields a Complete snapshot, which also fixes the record and the UI. Add a media hook that re-checks pending clip pulls with files.is_complete. Dropping `biased` is optional.
confirmed.verify: The missing recovery is real. Lagged is only logged (pump.rs:121), although files.rs:499-500 says a lagged receiver must re-query. A lost Completed{Attachment} means have_add never runs, and set_have only runs at start (app.rs:178), so the file is not announced until a restart. A lost final Transfer leaves the persisted download record stale. The UI transferStore also stays on the old state, because ensureTransfer only fetches unknown hashes (actions.ts:601-609). The starvation mechanism is not established, though. The biased select polls file_rx whenever net_rx is empty. The pump drains up to 2048 net events per batch, and per-message work in bulk is tiny. File events come at about 3 concurrent downloads plus one Queued per who_has round trip. A backlog of 512 needs a pump stall of several seconds, so the trigger is rare.

confirmed.title: Bulk window has no maximum length: steady traffic (or one spamming member) suppresses all live messages in a server
confirmed.scenario: Once a server goes bulk (more than 8 messages in one drain, or more than 40 per second), every further message pushes quiet_at to now+400ms (pump.rs:223-226). Bulk ends only when quiet_at passes (pump.rs:339-355), and there is no cap. No host rate limit exists in tincan-net. One untrusted member sends 41 messages in one second, then one message every 300 ms. Every member's pump stays in bulk indefinitely: no message-added for anyone's messages in any channel of that server, and dirty server, channel and member refreshes are deferred (pump.rs:366-369). Unread dots, the member list and online states for that server freeze. Each time the spammer pauses 400 ms, the bulk ends with a snapshot (pump.rs:349-351), which makes every UI drop all of its message caches (actions.ts applySnapshot `messages: {}`). Repeating this keeps every client reloading. A post-migration resync burst followed by busy chat freezes the view the same way, with no attacker.
confirmed.fix: Extend quiet_at only for messages that are part of a burst (over_rate is true, or the batch had more than BATCH_BULK messages for the conversation), so traffic below the threshold lets the window close. Add a hard maximum bulk duration (e.g. 5 s), after which the bulk ends with its snapshot and only a batch over BATCH_BULK can re-enter it. A flat cap alone would make a long legitimate sync flap, with a cache-dropping snapshot each cycle. A host-side per-member publish rate limit (tincan-net) is the real defence against floods.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. Every message in bulk pushes quiet_at to now+400 ms (pump.rs:223-226). Bulk ends only after 400 ms of silence (pump.rs:339-355), with no maximum. tincan-net has no publish rate limit. One member sends 41 messages in a second (over_rate counts per server, pump.rs:172-180), then one message every 300 ms. From then on every member's pump suppresses message-added for the whole server, and refreshes stay deferred (pump.rs:366-369). Each pause ends the bulk with a snapshot, which drops the UI's message caches (actions.ts:307). A post-migration catch-up followed by busy chat produces the same freeze without an attacker.

confirmed.title: Attachment index is first-writer-wins per hash, so downloads are routed to the wrong conversation (and the index can be poisoned)
confirmed.scenario: index_attachments uses atts.entry(hash).or_insert_with(..) (views.rs:343-346), so the first message seen with a hash sets conv, author, size and mime for all later uses. att_ref then serves that entry (transfers.rs:157-172), and start_download persists it and runs who_has(&att.conv) in that conversation only (transfers.rs:233,244). Requery (transfers.rs:121-127) reuses it. Example: Bob posts report.pdf (hash H) in server A and goes offline, and nobody in A fetched it. Carol posts the same file in server B and is online. V syncs A first, so A's entry wins and the auto-fetch goes Unavailable. Clicking Download on Carol's message in B (cmd_download) asks only A again, so the file never arrives although Carol holds it. A hostile peer can trigger the same thing on purpose: post a message in a DM to V claiming hash H with a fake size or mime before V indexes the real one. V's downloads of H then go only to the attacker's DM, and the attacker never serves.
confirmed.fix: Store hash -> a small list of AttRef (deduplicated by conversation, capped around 8) and persist it. In start_download, Requery and Peers, run who_has in every known conversation and merge the providers (all authors and holders, deduplicated). Take size, mime and name from the ref of the message the user acted on. Do not let an in-memory entry shadow a persisted one; merge them.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. or_insert_with makes the first message seen with a hash win (views.rs:343-346). att_ref, start_download, Requery and Peers all use that single conversation for who_has (transfers.rs:108-127,232-248). Holders are per server host, so a holder known only in conversation B is never asked. In-memory index entries also shadow the persisted record after a restart (att_ref checks memory first, transfers.rs:158), and start_download then overwrites the persisted origin. The trigger needs the same file in two conversations with the first-indexed copy unfetchable, which auto-fetch makes uncommon. The hostile variant needs the attacker to know the hash in advance. Hence low.

confirmed.title: view() cache can store a stale ConvView that was built before a concurrent invalidation
confirmed.scenario: On a miss, view() clones net.conv_state outside the lock and inserts the result afterwards (views.rs:158-166). Race: a command thread misses and clones the old state S0. The session then ingests a Members or Channels change and emits ConvUpdated. The pump invalidates (nothing cached yet) and its update_policy rebuilds and inserts S1. The command thread then inserts S0 over S1. Every later refresh, channels/members command and update_policy uses S0: a new channel missing, a new member missing from members-updated. This lasts until the next non-message change for that conversation. The window is small but recurs on every invalidation while UI commands run on other runtime workers (3 workers).
confirmed.fix: Keep a per-conversation generation counter that invalidate_view bumps. view() reads the generation before calling conv_state and inserts only if it is unchanged; otherwise it returns the freshly built Arc without caching it.
confirmed.verify: Real. Tauri async commands run concurrently on the 3-worker runtime (src-tauri main.rs:65-66, commands.rs:16), and the pump runs on another worker. The race is simpler than described. A command thread misses and clones the old state. The change is ingested and invalidate_view removes nothing. The command thread then inserts the stale view (views.rs:158-166). The pump's debounced refresh 100 ms later reads that stale view, so channels-updated and members-updated miss the change until the next non-message change. The window is only the conv_state clone plus the build, so it is rare.

confirmed.title: A rename made while a Profile publish is in flight is dropped
confirmed.scenario: ensure_profile returns early while profile_inflight holds the server (app.rs:313-315). The spawned task publishes the name captured at spawn time and then just clears the flag (app.rs:316-322). Publish waits up to 15 s while connecting (timing.rs publish_timeout). The user sets name A while the server is connecting, then corrects it to B. set_name(B) skips the server because A is in flight. on_connected also skips it, since A is still queued. A is then acked. Other members see A, my profile says B, and nothing retries until the next ConnectionChanged (host migration or restart).
confirmed.fix: In the spawned task, after removing the inflight mark, call core.ensure_profile(server) again. Or loop: publish while core.name differs from the name just published.
confirmed.verify: Real, but it partly self-heals. The early return on profile_inflight (app.rs:313-315) drops the second rename, and the task only clears the flag (app.rs:316-322). The only other trigger is ConnectionChanged. tincan-net emits it also on material RTT or path changes while Member (session/mod.rs:1424-1439), so a member on a moving path republishes the current name soon after. A host or solo node (rtt None, path None, host.rs:202-209), or a member on a stable LAN, keeps the stale name until a migration or restart.

confirmed.title: My own DM messages never refresh DmSummary.lastMessageAt, so the DM list order goes stale
confirmed.scenario: The pump marks a refresh only for messages not authored by me (pump.rs:228-230), and cmd_send_message (commands.rs:219-243) emits nothing for the DM summary. The UI sorts DMs by lastMessageAt (DmSidebar.tsx:13) and never updates it locally. After I write to an older DM, it stays below more recent ones until some unrelated DM refresh happens (a DmLinkUp/Down or roster flush).
confirmed.fix: In the pump, mark Refresh { dm: true } for a DM conversation on every Change::Message, whatever the author; only the unread part depends on the author. Alternatively, call refresh(conv, Refresh { dm: true }) after a successful DM publish in cmd_send_message.
confirmed.verify: Real, but it self-heals. My own messages are not marked (pump.rs:228-230), cmd_send_message emits no dm-updated, the UI never updates lastMessageAt (only the mock does), and markSeen skips my own messages (actions.ts:251). Several things repair it. Every member's Status every 30 s makes the host broadcast a roster (host.rs:767-770), and each RosterUpdated sets dms_dirty and refresh_dms. A send that dials an idle link fires DmLinkUp, which refreshes the DM. So the order is stale for up to about 30 s while in a connected server with others. It stays stale only for DM-only or lone profiles, or when the link is already up and no roster change follows.

confirmed.title: DM names and DM author names depend on which server views happen to be cached
confirmed.scenario: user_name looks only at server views already in the cache (views.rs:187-189) and otherwise falls back to the contact record, which is written once at DM-open time and is often the short id. Server views are invalidated on every ConvUpdated, and during a bulk sync they are not rebuilt until the bulk ends (update_policy is deferred, pump.rs:260-265). While that lasts, message-added and typing for DMs from a peer known only through that server carry the short id as authorName or name, as does a snapshot built then. The UI keeps that authorName in its message cache. A flush that refreshes a DM before its server (HashMap order, pump.rs:365-371) also emits dm-updated with the fallback name.
confirmed.fix: In user_name, resolve through self.view(&conv) for the server conversations in net.convs(), which rebuilds on a miss, or keep a UserId -> name directory updated on every ConvView build and never invalidated. Also update the contact record's name when a server name is learned.
confirmed.verify: Real, but narrower than claimed. update_policy is not deferred until the bulk ends: flush handles policy_dirty on every flush (pump.rs:373-376), which rebuilds every view within about 100 ms of a Members change. Only Channels and ServerRenamed invalidations during bulk leave the server view uncached until the bulk ends or something calls view(). In those windows user_name falls back to the contact record (views.rs:187-194). That record usually holds a real name written at DM open; it is the short id only when written in such a window or by add_contact. The bulk-end snapshot drops the UI message caches, so wrong authorNames self-heal. What remains is a transient cosmetic wrong name in typing and dm-updated, plus a possibly short-id contact record.

confirmed.title: Leave voice while an outgoing call rings only cancels the call; the user stays in the room with a live mic while the UI shows them as gone
confirmed.scenario: You can call someone while you are in a voice room: MemberList.tsx:50 and ChatView.tsx:51 only block calling when s.call is set or voice.kind is "call". While the call rings out, CallPanel.tsx:26 shows the room panel, because "Cancel call" only appears when there is no voice session. Its only button is "Leave voice", which calls leaveVoice(). leaveVoice checks `s.voice?.kind === "call" || s.call`, and s.call is the ringing call, so it sends call_hangup. Media::call_hangup (session.rs:668) calls Net::call_hangup. hub.rs:618 hangup calls end_call, which ends the call but leaves st.room alone, so the room session keeps running: engine attached, mic sending, status.voice still set. The .then() then patches `voice: null, call: null`. The backend's voice DTO has not changed, and emit_voice (session.rs:366-374) only sends on a change, so no voice-updated arrives to correct the UI. Result: the voice panel disappears and the user thinks they left, but the room still hears their mic. The member list even keeps showing them in the voice channel. This lasts until some unrelated change re-sends voice-updated.
confirmed.fix: In actions.ts leaveVoice, branch on the voice session, not on s.call. If s.voice?.kind === 'call' || (!s.voice && s.call), invoke call_hangup and patch { voice: null, call: null, soundboardOpen: false, fullStage: false }. Else if s.voice (a room), invoke voice_leave and patch only { voice: null, soundboardOpen: false, fullStage: false }, keeping s.call. Net::voice_leave with a ringing-out call (state not Active) only stops the room, and Media::voice_leave keeps pending_call, so the call keeps ringing and CallPanel switches to its 'Calling / Cancel call' view. Also add a cancel control to the room CallPanel when voice && call?.state === 'ringing-out'. It should call a cancelCall() that invokes call_hangup and patches only call: null, so a ringing call can be cancelled without touching the room.
confirmed.verify: I checked the whole path and it holds. While you are in a room, ChatView.tsx:51 and MemberList.tsx:50 only block calling when s.call is set or voice.kind is 'call', so you can ring someone. Net::call_start (hub.rs:525-567) leaves st.room alone. CallPanel.tsx:26 only shows 'Cancel call' when !voice, so during the ring the panel's only red button is 'Leave voice', which runs leaveVoice(). actions.ts:647 then sees s.call set and sends call_hangup. Media::call_hangup (session.rs:668-673) calls Net hangup, and end_call (hub.rs:702-715) only takes st.call and stops the call's own handle; the room handle stays in st.room. reconcile still sees voice_info() == room (active() falls back to room), so it does not detach. emit_voice dedupes against last_voice, so no voice-updated is sent. The .then() patches voice: null, call: null. Result: the mic stays live in the room, status.voice stays set and others still see and hear you, while the UI shows no voice session. Nothing corrects it until the voice DTO changes: rosters are only re-sent on change (debounced), and ConnectionChanged only fires on a 25% RTT move. That can take minutes in a quiet room. The ringing-in variant cannot happen because IncomingCallDialog is modal. This is high because the Leave button fails silently and leaves an open mic.

confirmed.title: reconcile reads voice_info/call_info before taking the state lock, so a stale read can detach a room that was just joined
confirmed.scenario: reconcile reads `core.net.voice_info()` and `core.net.call_info()` before `self.st.lock()`. Net::voice_join (hub.rs:420-447) emits events before the new room is installed. Switching rooms emits VoiceUpdated(old) after `room.take()`. Joining from an active call makes hangup emit VoiceUpdated and CallUpdated(Ended). In both cases the new room is set later by `st.room.replace(handle)`. The pump task wakes on those events and calls reconcile, which can read voice_info() == None inside that window. It then blocks on the hub lock in call_info() while voice_join holds it to spawn the new room. Meanwhile the command task continues from the hub unlock straight into Media::voice_join's locked block (session.rs:578-587): it calls sw.finish, which drops switching to 0, then attach_locked for room B. When the pump finally takes st, it sees switching == 0, attached = Room B and the stale info None, so `stale` is true and detach_locked runs: stop_call, audio/video pumps aborted, audio_out dropped. reconcile never re-attaches rooms, only pending calls. voice_join still returns the Ok(dto) it computed before that detach, so the UI patches voice = room B (actions.ts:637-640). Net keeps me in room B (status.voice set, others see me), but no audio is sent or received, and rejoining from the UI is the only way out.
confirmed.fix: In Media::reconcile, take `let mut st = self.st.lock();` first, then read `let info = core.net.voice_info(); let call = core.net.call_info();` while holding it. A reconcile that gets st before a command's finish block then sees switching > 0. One that gets st after it reads Net state from after the Net call returned, which already has the new room installed.
confirmed.verify: The race is real, though the timing window is narrow. reconcile (session.rs:221-223) reads core.net.voice_info() and call_info() before self.st.lock(). In hub.rs voice_join (414-448), VoiceUpdated{old} is emitted after room.take(), and hangup emits VoiceUpdated/CallUpdated(Ended) when joining from a call. Both happen before set_status and the hub-locked voice::spawn and room.replace, so voice_info() returns None in between. The pump handles these events in its own task (pump.rs:322 -> media.on_net_event -> reconcile). If the pump reads info=None in that window and then parks on the hub lock in call_info() while voice_join holds it for spawn, the command thread keeps running. It unlocks, emits, returns and takes st first (session.rs:578-587: sw.finish sets switching to 0, attach_locked(Room B)). The pump then takes st with stale info None and detach_locked runs. reconcile never re-attaches rooms, only pending calls, and voice_join already computed Ok(dto). The result is that Net keeps me in room B, visible to others, with no audio until I leave and rejoin. Taking st first is safe for lock order: voice_dto and live_tracks already take the hub lock while holding st, and Net never calls back into Media. Medium because it needs a tight interleaving, but the failure is silent when it hits.

confirmed.title: Heard clips are capped at 50 in the app but the UI appends every sound-played clip without limit; older tiles can't be saved
confirmed.scenario: on_sound calls `st.heard.put(heard)`, which drops the oldest entry past MAX_HEARD = 50 (clips.rs:32, 62-68), but it emits only sound-played, never clips-updated. The UI's sound-played listener (actions.ts:399-402) appends every unseen hash to s.clips. In a long session where more than 50 different clips are played, the soundboard keeps tiles the backend has forgotten. Clicking save on one runs clip_fetch, which fails with "That sound is no longer available." (clips.rs:403). A hostile room member can also send SoundPlayed with random hashes at any rate: the SFU forwards them with no rate limit (sfu.rs:506-520), and each one passes the size/duration check and grows the UI's clip list and its play timers until the next clips-updated, which only comes on detach, add, remove, rename or transfer progress.
confirmed.fix: In actions.ts, make the sound-played handler mirror Heard::put for non-owned clips. Call markPlaying. If clip.owned is false, remove any existing entry with that hash, push it at the end, then drop the oldest non-owned entries beyond 50 (the same MAX_HEARD). Owned entries are unchanged. Optionally, add a per-sender throttle in Media::on_sound, for example ignore a user's announcements closer than 250 ms apart, kept in State and cleared on detach, so a flood costs neither the IPC nor the store.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. on_sound (clips.rs:375-396) caps st.heard at MAX_HEARD=50 via Heard::put but emits only sound-played. The UI handler (actions.ts:399-402) appends every unseen hash with an O(n) .some() scan plus an O(n) array copy. clips-updated only comes on detach (when heard is non-empty), clip_add/remove/rename, clip_fetch, on_clip_transfer (only for fetching or heard hashes) and finish_fetch. Normal use: after more than 50 different heard clips in one session, older tiles stay in the UI and Save fails with 'That sound is no longer available.' (clips.rs:403). Hostile use: an admitted room member can send SoundPlayed with random hashes and small claimed sizes, which pass the size/duration check. The app adds no rate limit, and the SFU and voice paths in net forward them without one. The UI list then grows without bound for the whole voice session, with quadratic copying, until the UI is sluggish. It resets on leaving voice. markPlaying timers are not a leak: they are per-hash and clear themselves. The proposed backend fix (emit clips-updated on every new heard entry) would cost a list_clips storage read and a transfer lookup per hash during a flood, so the cap belongs in the UI.

confirmed.title: clip_fetch on an already-held blob that can't be read or tagged leaves a persisted pull that never resolves and looks complete
confirmed.scenario: clip_fetch inserts the hash into st.fetching and persists it to kv app/clip_fetches. If core.files.is_complete(hash) is true, it calls read_to_bytes(hash, MAX_CLIP_BYTES) and then import_bytes. If the read fails (the held attachment is larger than 5 MiB, which a peer can trigger by announcing a big attachment's hash with a small claimed size, or the disk read fails) or the import fails, the code only logs a warning. No Completed{Clip} event fires, so finish_fetch never runs and the fetching entry is never removed, even across restarts (load_fetches). The returned tile uses transfer_of(), and Files::transfer reports a held blob as Complete, so the UI shows the clip as downloaded but it never enters the library and no error is shown.
confirmed.fix: In clip_fetch's is_complete branch, on read_to_bytes or import_bytes failure, lock st, remove the hash from st.fetching, call save_fetches, and return Err. For Err(FilesError::TooLarge { .. }) use 'That sound is larger than 5 MB, so it wasn't saved.' and also remove it from st.heard and emit clips-updated. For any other error use 'Couldn't save the sound. Try again.'. To cover a blob already tagged as Clip but not in the library, where import_bytes adds no new kind and no Completed fires: if import succeeds but the hash is still in st.fetching and the blob already had the Clip kind, call finish_fetch directly.
confirmed.verify: The path is real, but the claimed outcome is a little off. clip_fetch (clips.rs:404-418) persists the fetch, then for an already-held blob calls read_to_bytes(hash, MAX_CLIP_BYTES). That returns FilesError::TooLarge for a blob over 5 MiB (files.rs:389-393). A peer can trigger this by announcing a big held attachment's hash with a small claimed size, because on_sound only checks the claimed size. The read error, or an import_bytes error, is only logged. The success path does work: mark_held returns newly added kinds, so Completed{Clip} fires and finish_fetch runs. On the failure path no Completed event fires, so the st.fetching entry and the kv app/clip_fetches entry stay forever. Media::start reloads them, and nothing resumes a complete blob. Files::transfer reports the held blob as Complete, but HeardTile (Soundboard.tsx:51-72) only hides Save while downloading or queued. So the UI does not show it as downloaded: Save stays visible and silently does nothing each time it is clicked. The impact is one stale kv entry per hash and a dead Save button, so low.

confirmed.title: Windows logoff, shutdown and Restart Manager exit without App::shutdown (no host handoff, store not flushed)
confirmed.scenario: The run closure (main.rs:96-103) handles only RunEvent::ExitRequested { code: None }. When Windows signs out or shuts down, it sends WM_QUERYENDSESSION and then WM_ENDSESSION. tao 0.37.3 does not process the first (DefWindowProc returns TRUE). In the WM_ENDSESSION handler (platform_impl/windows/event_loop.rs:2346-2357) it calls event_loop_runner.loop_destroyed(), which goes through move_state_to(Destroyed) to Event::LoopDestroyed, then tauri-runtime-wry RunEvent::Exit, then the shell callback (tauri app.rs:1449-1452). It then calls std::process::exit(0) directly. No CloseRequested or ExitRequested event fires, so begin_close never runs and App::shutdown is skipped. Restart Manager (for example Windows Update restarting apps) takes the same path. Concrete case: a user hosting a server, or with an attachment downloading, shuts down the PC with Tincan open. There is no clean handoff, so members wait for crash-failover timeouts with a longer text and voice interruption. net.shutdown, router.shutdown and Files::shutdown never run, so download progress is lost. architecture.md:224 says a hard kill loses the last partial chunk, and docs/research/iroh.facts.md:26 measured that a hard exit early in a download lost all of its progress.
confirmed.fix: In gate.rs add `pub fn try_get(&self) -> Option<T> { match &*self.rx.borrow() { Phase::Ready(v) => Some(v.clone()), _ => None } }`. In Shell add `exiting: AtomicBool`, and set it at the top of exit_now (`if let Some(s) = handle.try_state::<Shell>() { s.exiting.store(true, Ordering::Release) }`). In the app.run closure add an arm: `RunEvent::Exit => { if let Some(shell) = handle.try_state::<Shell>() { if !shell.exiting.load(Ordering::Acquire) { if let Some(app) = shell.gate.try_get() { tauri::async_runtime::block_on(async move { let _ = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(4), app.shutdown()).await; }); } } } }`. This runs only when the loop is destroyed by something other than Tincan's own exit sequence (WM_ENDSESSION or Restart Manager). It joins a begin_close shutdown already in progress (OnceCell waiters wait), and it does not re-run a shutdown that already timed out. It stays inside Windows' roughly 5 s end-session allowance. Note that files.shutdown is the last step, so a slow handoff can push the store flush past the 4 s cap.
confirmed.verify: I traced the whole path and it holds. tao 0.37.3 handles WM_ENDSESSION only in thread_event_target_callback (platform_impl/windows/event_loop.rs:2346-2357). The thread event target window is a top-level WS_VISIBLE|WS_POPUP layered window with no parent and no HWND_MESSAGE (event_loop.rs:650-688), so Windows delivers WM_QUERYENDSESSION and WM_ENDSESSION to it. WM_QUERYENDSESSION is not handled. On WM_ENDSESSION(TRUE) it calls runner.loop_destroyed(), which goes through move_state_to(Destroyed) to Event::LoopDestroyed, then tauri-runtime-wry lib.rs:4134 RunEvent::Exit, then the shell callback (tauri app.rs:1449-1452) and cleanup_before_exit. After that it calls std::process::exit(0) directly. CloseRequested and ExitRequested never fire, so main.rs:99 never matches, begin_close never runs and App::shutdown (app.rs:243-266) is skipped. There is no suspend, logoff or ENDSESSION handling anywhere else in the repo. Effect: when the host signs out or shuts down the PC, which is the most common way a long-running chat app stops, no Handoff is sent and the QUIC connections drop without a HOST_LEAVING close. Members only declare the host dead after 10 s of silence and then go through succession dials (architecture.md:170,185), instead of switching at once (architecture.md:183). The data-loss part is overstated: SQLite commits are durable. Only recent partial download progress since the last store flush is lost (architecture.md:224, notes-tincan-files.md:10), though a download that has just started can lose all of it (iroh.facts.md:26). The proposed fix works. Handle::block_on enters the runtime, so tokio::time works inside the async block. Shutdown does not wait on the main thread: emits and Channel sends are posted to the event loop proxy. try_get returns None for Starting and Failed. One flaw: on the normal path, begin_close's 5 s timeout drops the get_or_init future, which cancels the tokio OnceCell initialisation. The proposed Exit arm would then restart the whole shutdown sequence after exit_now, until the EXIT_GRACE thread kills the process 3 s later.

confirmed.title: Uninstaller's 'Delete the application data' option leaves every Tincan profile (identity key, messages, files) on disk
confirmed.scenario: The Tauri 2.12.6 NSIS template (embedded in the CLI binary) handles that checkbox like this: `${If} $DeleteAppDataCheckboxState = 1 ${AndIf} $UpdateMode <> 1 ... RmDir /r "$APPDATA\${BUNDLEID}"` and `RmDir /r "$LOCALAPPDATA\${BUNDLEID}"`. That deletes %APPDATA%\app.tincan.desktop and %LOCALAPPDATA%\app.tincan.desktop. Tincan keeps everything under %APPDATA%\Tincan\profiles\<name>\ (main.rs:134-135, profile.rs:45). That covers identity.key, the SQLite message history, the blob store with every downloaded attachment and clip, and the WebView2 data folder (profile.rs:50-51, which also moves WebView2 out of the bundle-id folder). A user who uninstalls and ticks 'Delete the application data' keeps all of it. Reinstalling later silently brings back the old identity and history.
confirmed.fix: In tauri.conf.json add `"installerHooks": "./windows/hooks.nsh"` under bundle.windows.nsis (the path is relative to src-tauri). Put this in src-tauri/windows/hooks.nsh: `!macro NSIS_HOOK_POSTUNINSTALL` / `${If} $DeleteAppDataCheckboxState = 1` / `${AndIf} $UpdateMode <> 1` / `SetShellVarContext current` / `RmDir /r "$APPDATA\Tincan"` / `${EndIf}` / `!macroend`. RmDir /r is best-effort. A msedgewebview2.exe child that outlives the killed app can briefly hold files in profiles\<name>\webview, so a second RmDir after a short Sleep makes it more reliable.
confirmed.verify: I confirmed this in the template embedded in the installed CLI binary (@tauri-apps/cli-win32-x64-msvc 2.12.6). Under `${If} $DeleteAppDataCheckboxState = 1 ${AndIf} $UpdateMode <> 1` it runs only `SetShellVarContext current`, `RmDir /r "$APPDATA\${BUNDLEID}"` and `RmDir /r "$LOCALAPPDATA\${BUNDLEID}"`, which here means app.tincan.desktop. Right after that it runs `!ifmacrodef NSIS_HOOK_POSTUNINSTALL !insertmacro NSIS_HOOK_POSTUNINSTALL !endif`, and the template has `!include "{{installer_hooks}}"`. Tincan keeps everything in roaming %APPDATA%\Tincan\profiles\<name> (main.rs:134-135, profile.rs:44-52), including the WebView2 data folder through .data_directory (main.rs:163), and no docs say the data is kept on purpose. A user who ticks 'Delete the application data' keeps identity.key (the private identity), the full message and DM history and every cached blob. A reinstall silently brings back the old identity. The hook placement and variable scope in the proposed fix are correct: NSIS Vars are global and LogicLib is already included.

confirmed.title: Relaunching during the close window, or a plain double launch, ends with an 'already running' dialog and nothing on screen
confirmed.scenario: begin_close hides the window at once (main.rs:222-223). The profile lock is released only at the end of App::shutdown (app.rs:262), after the handoff, which takes about 3 s in practice (notes-tincan-app.md:62) and up to the 5 s SHUTDOWN_CAP. Concrete case: a user closes Tincan and relaunches it right away, for example after the app's own 'restart Tincan' error text. The new process creates a window first (main.rs:138), App::start fails at profile::lock with 'Tincan is already running with this profile.', and fatal hides the new window and shows that dialog (main.rs:185-187). No Tincan window is visible and the user has to guess to retry later. A normal double launch while Tincan runs gives the same dialog and never brings the running window forward.
confirmed.fix: In start(), when App::start returns the already-running error, do two things. (1) Enumerate top-level windows (EnumWindows) for one titled profile::window_title(&name), owned by a different PID (GetWindowThreadProcessId != std::process::id()) and visible (IsWindowVisible). If one exists, it is a genuine running instance: ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE) and SetForegroundWindow it, then exit_now(&handle, 0) without a dialog. (2) If none is visible, the other instance is in its hidden closing phase: retry App::start every 250 ms for up to SHUTDOWN_CAP + EXIT_GRACE, and only then call fatal. Export the text as `pub const ALREADY_RUNNING` from tincan-app's lib.rs, or better a distinct error kind, instead of matching a literal in the shell.
confirmed.verify: The race is real but narrow. begin_close hides the window at once (main.rs:222-223). The profile lock (File::try_lock, crates/tincan-app/src/profile.rs:32-45) is released only at app.rs:262, at the end of a shutdown that takes about 3 s in practice and is capped at 5 s. profile::lock is the first step of Core::start (app.rs:134). A relaunch inside that window therefore opens a window, fails with ALREADY_RUNNING, then fatal hides that window and shows the dialog (main.rs:185-210). The user sees an 'already running' dialog with no Tincan window anywhere. The plain double-launch part is designed and documented (notes-tincan-app.md:32), and its text is accurate, so that part is not a defect. The proposed fix has flaws. FindWindowW by title can return the new process's own window, which main.rs:138 creates with the same title before App::start. An unconditional 8 s retry makes a genuine double launch sit behind an empty loading window for 8 s. ALREADY_RUNNING is pub(crate), so the shell cannot share it without a contract addition.

confirmed.title: Leave voice in a room hangs up a pending call instead, then marks voice null while the mic stays live in the room
confirmed.scenario: You are in voice room General. You click Call on Bob (the DmChat call button and the MemberList Call item are both enabled in a room because busy only counts voice.kind === 'call'), so s.call is ringing-out. CallPanel still shows the room panel and its 'Leave voice' button, which calls leaveVoice(). leaveVoice picks call_hangup because s.call is set. Media::call_hangup -> Net hangup only ends the call (hub.rs hangup: CallEnd/Cancelled) and does not touch st.room. reconcile keeps the room attached, and emit_voice sends nothing because the DTO has not changed (any voice-updated it does send comes before the command response). Then `.then(() => patch({ voice: null, call: null, ... }))` clears voice in the UI. Result: the UI says you left, but the engine keeps sending your mic to the room and others still see and hear you.
confirmed.fix: Route on what voice is: `if (s.voice?.kind === 'room') run(invoke('voice_leave', {}).then(() => patch({ voice: null, soundboardOpen: false, fullStage: false })));` `else if (s.voice?.kind === 'call' || s.call) run(invoke('call_hangup', {}).then(() => patch({ voice: null, call: null, soundboardOpen: false, fullStage: false })));`. Net voice_leave hangs up only an Active call, so a ringing-out call survives leaving the room, and CallPanel then shows its existing 'Calling … Cancel call' panel. Also show the ringing-out state and a separate Cancel button inside the room panel, so cancelling the call never needs the room's leave button.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed end to end. ChatView.tsx:51 and MemberList.tsx:50 count only call !== null or voice.kind === 'call' as busy, so Call is enabled while you are in a room. Net hub.rs call_start allows ringing out from a room; activate() leaves the room only on accept. While ringing out, s.voice is the room and s.call is ringing-out, so CallPanel shows the room panel. Its 'Leave voice' calls leaveVoice, and actions.ts:647 picks call_hangup because s.call is set. Media::call_hangup (session.rs:668) leads to hub.rs hangup, which ends only the call (Cancelled). reconcile does not see the room as stale: State::active() (hub.rs:85-89) returns the room unless the call is Active. emit_voice dedups an unchanged DTO, so no voice-updated is sent, and then .then patches voice:null. The engine keeps sending the mic to the room while the UI shows no voice session. Nothing corrects it until the next roster, material RTT or mute change, or a snapshot. Ringing-in is mostly blocked because IncomingCallDialog is a modal, so the trigger is calling someone from a room and clicking Leave voice during the ring (up to 45 s). Severity is high because the mic stays live without the user knowing.

confirmed.title: message-added and message-updated that arrive while a conversation's first page loads are dropped; the message is also marked read
confirmed.scenario: You open channel A, so ensureMessages invokes `messages`. The backend reads storage at T0, a new message M is stored at T1, and its message-added reaches the UI before the page response. putMessage finds no s.messages[key] entry and returns, dropping M. markSeen still runs, finds A on screen, and calls mark_read. The page from T0 then lands with loaded:true and no M. M never appears until a snapshot or restart, and it no longer shows as unread. The 'live' merge in ensureMessages (lines 142-149) is dead code, because no unloaded entry is ever created. The same applies to a DM delivery ack (message-updated pending:false) or a delete in that window: the message stays 'Waiting for X to come online' or stays visible.
confirmed.fix: In putMessage, when there is no entry and inflight.has(`msgs:${key}`), create `{ list: [m], cursor: null, loaded: false, loadingOlder: false }` (ensureMessages proceeds because it checks .loaded). In ensureMessages, merge page and live by id with the one-way rule (`pending: a.pending && b.pending, deleted: a.deleted || b.deleted`) instead of letting the page copy win. Then sort by sentAt. When page.cursor !== null, drop live-only entries older than page.messages[0].sentAt: a message-updated for an older message would otherwise land at the end of the list.
confirmed.verify: The mechanics hold. An entry in s.messages is created only when ensureMessages lands, with loaded:true (loadOlder and setLoading only touch existing entries). putMessage (actions.ts:195) therefore drops any message-added or message-updated that arrives while the first page is in flight, and the 'live' merge at 142-149 is dead code. cmd_messages is a synchronous storage read (dispatch.rs:232). pump.rs:227 emits message-added right after storage. Tauri gives no ordering between an IPC response and an emitted event. markSeen still calls mark_read, and the backend marks read up to the newest stored message, so the dropped message is also not unread. The entry is never reloaded except by a snapshot or restart. The window is only the gap between a local read and its IPC delivery (about a millisecond or so), so this is rare, but when it hits a message is silently hidden and marked read for the whole session. The same window drops a DM ack (pending stays true) or a delete.

confirmed.title: Composer erases text typed while a send is in flight
confirmed.scenario: send() leaves the textarea enabled and awaits send_message. For servers, Net::publish returns only after the host acks, which is a relay round trip (100-300 ms) or much longer while the host is migrating; DMs and attachments add import time. You press Enter and keep typing the next message, which goes after the old text still in the box. When the ack returns, setText('') and drafts.delete(key) wipe everything, including what you typed after. Pressing Enter again during the send does nothing (sending guard), so a fast second message is silently lost.
confirmed.fix: Clear the box when the send starts and restore it only on failure: `const raw = text, sentFiles = files; setText(''); setFiles([]); drafts.delete(key);` then await. In catch: `setText(cur => (cur === '' ? raw : cur)); setFiles(f => (f.length === 0 ? sentFiles : f)); if (raw) drafts.set(key, raw);` plus setError. Do not strip a startsWith prefix: that duplicates or mangles text when the user edits during the send. Optionally queue an Enter pressed during a send and run it when the send finishes instead of ignoring it.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. The textarea stays enabled during send. send() awaits sendMessage, and for servers Net::publish returns only after the host acks (net.rs:365: a relay round trip, longer during migration); attachments add import time. Text typed meanwhile goes into state and drafts. On success, setText('') and drafts.delete(key) wipe it. A second Enter during the send hits the `sending` guard and does nothing. Sending two short messages in quick succession is common chat behaviour, so the second message is silently lost.

confirmed.title: Page responses that started before a snapshot are merged into the reloaded cache, leaving a permanent hole
confirmed.scenario: You scroll far back in a channel, so loadOlder captures `before = cursor` from several pages deep. A snapshot arrives (bulk catch-up ended, a join, or lag). applySnapshot sets messages to {}, and afterViewChange reloads the newest page. If that newest page lands before the older page, loadOlder's update finds `c` (the fresh 30-message entry), prepends the deep older page, and sets the cursor from it. Everything between the two pages is missing, and paging never fills it. The same gap affects ensureMessages: a pre-snapshot `msgs:key` load still in flight blocks the post-snapshot reload through once(), then lands with data read before the snapshot.
confirmed.fix: In loadOlder's update use `if (!c || c.cursor !== before) return s;` (the fresh entry already has loadingOlder:false). For ensureMessages, add a module-level cacheGen that applySnapshot increments when wasReady. Capture it when the request starts, and if it changed when the page lands, discard the page and call ensureMessages(convId, channelId) again after the once() finally.
confirmed.verify: The path exists. loadOlder's update (actions.ts:171-179) checks only that an entry exists, not that it is the same one, so a deep older page that lands after a snapshot's fresh newest page is prepended above it, the cursor jumps, and the gap is never filled. Two local `messages` reads have to complete or be delivered out of order, so this is a narrow race. The ensureMessages part is real only for lag snapshots. After a bulk-end snapshot the in-flight read happened at least 400 ms after the last bulk message, so it is complete. The once() guard does block the post-snapshot reload, though.

confirmed.title: Every snapshot drops the cache of the conversation on screen, which loses the reading position
confirmed.scenario: You are scrolled back reading history in server Y. A short network blip makes server X catch up more than 8 messages, which counts as bulk; after it goes quiet the pump emits a snapshot. applySnapshot sets messages to {} for all conversations. MessageList's conv becomes undefined (rows empty, scrollTop 0), then only the newest page comes back. stick is false, so you are left near the top of the newest page, and your place in Y is gone because of an unrelated server.
confirmed.fix: In applySnapshot, keep the cache of the conversation on screen and drop the others. Then fetch its newest page. If the page overlaps the cached list by id, replace the overlapping tail with the page copies and keep the older cached part and its cursor. If there is no overlap, replace the whole list as now. That keeps it hole-safe while preserving the scroll position in the common case.
confirmed.verify: The mechanics hold. applySnapshot sets messages to {} on every snapshot after the first (actions.ts:307). The pump emits one after bulk ingest in any conversation, joins, leaves and lag (pump.rs:349,299,309,189). MessageList's conv becomes undefined (rows empty, scrollTop clamps to 0), and only the newest page returns with stick false, so the reading position in an unrelated conversation is lost. The drop is deliberate (comment at actions.ts:305-307, events.rs header) to avoid holes after dropped events. That makes this a UX cost of the design, not a logic error, and any fix must keep that hole safety.

confirmed.title: Each typing event restarts the sweep timer, so a typer who stopped stays listed while someone else keeps typing
confirmed.scenario: Alice sends one typing event at t=0 (until t=6 s), then stops without sending. Bob types continuously, and sendTyping fires every 3 s. Each of Bob's events runs clearTimeout(prev) and schedules a new sweep 6 s later, so the sweep never runs while Bob types. 'Alice and Bob are typing' stays on screen for as long as Bob types.
confirmed.fix: Arm a sweep only when none is pending: `if (!typingTimers.has(key)) typingTimers.set(key, setTimeout(sweep, TYPING_SHOW_MS));`. Hoist sweep to a function of key. It already reschedules itself for the earliest remaining `until`.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. onTyping (actions.ts:334-336) clears and re-arms the per-conversation sweep timer for 6 s on every event. sendTyping throttles a typer to one event every 3 s, so while Bob types the sweep never fires. TypingLine and ChannelChat render s.typing[key] without filtering by `until`, so Alice stays listed until Bob stops for 6 s or Alice's own message removes her.

confirmed.title: The load-older scroll anchor is used up by a new message at the bottom, so the older page prepends without compensation
confirmed.scenario: You scroll to the top and requestOlder sets anchor.current. Before the older page arrives, a message-added changes rows, and the layout effect applies the anchor (keeping the distance from the bottom) and clears it. The older page then prepends 30 messages with anchor null and stick false, so the content you were reading jumps down by a whole page. This is plausible in any active channel while you scroll back.
confirmed.fix: Track prevFirst in a ref. In the layout effect, if anchor.current !== null and firstKey === prevFirst.current (append or in-place update), re-capture `anchor.current = el.scrollHeight - el.scrollTop` instead of applying it. Re-capturing beats just skipping: it keeps the distance exact even though a message was added at the bottom. Apply and clear it only when firstKey changed, then set prevFirst.current = firstKey.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed, and the stylesheet sets overflow-anchor: none on .msg-scroller, so the browser does not compensate. setLoading(true) leaves `list` unchanged, so the layout effect does not run, and the anchor stays pending. Any list change before the page lands (message-added, message-updated) changes rows. The effect then applies the anchor (shifting the view by the new message's height) and nulls it. The prepend then runs with anchor null and stick false, so the view jumps down by a whole page. The window is a local `messages` round trip, so it is occasional, in busy channels.

confirmed.title: An unsupported codec never shows the 'can't decode' error; the decoder is rebuilt and fails again at every keyframe
confirmed.scenario: A sharer (an untrusted peer, or an unusual GPU encoder) sends an SPS with a well-formed but unsupported profile, such as High 4:4:4 avc1.f4001f. VideoDecoder.configure() does not throw for this. It closes the decoder later through the error callback with NotSupportedError. The try/catch in configure() only catches TypeError, so onError just resets state. At the next keyframe (every 4 s, or as often as a peer sends them) a new decoder is built and fails again. The viewer shows 'Waiting for the first frame' forever and never the message at line 112.
confirmed.fix: In onError, `if (err.name === 'NotSupportedError')`: if the failed config used 'prefer-hardware', retry once with hardwareAcceleration 'no-preference' for that codec. Otherwise remember the failed codec, call onStatus({ kind: 'error', text: "This screen share uses a video format this PC can't decode." }), and skip configure for that codec string. Keep the current reset-at-next-keyframe behaviour for other errors such as EncodingError. Alternatively, `await VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported(cfg)` before configuring a new codec string, and drop frames until it resolves.
confirmed.verify: This holds per the WebCodecs spec; I could not run it. configure() throws TypeError only for an invalid config. An unsupported but well-formed config closes the decoder through the error callback with NotSupportedError. onError (ScreenView.tsx:137) only resets decoder, codec and needKey. At the next keyframe, `codec !== this.codec` (null) triggers configure again, which fails again, and status stays 'waiting' forever. codecFromAnnexB copies any SPS profile bytes, so a peer can cause this. More realistically, Chromium is reported to treat hardwareAcceleration 'prefer-hardware' as hardware-only, so a PC without a hardware H.264 decoder (VM, RDP, blocklisted GPU) could hit the same silent loop. I could not confirm that here.

confirmed.title: No hang-up control when the call is active but no voice session is attached
confirmed.scenario: You accept a call and attach fails, for example when AudioEngine::new errors. Media::call_accept returns Err (shown as a toast), but Net already sent CallAccept and set the call active. call-updated sets s.call to active, and voice stays null. CallPanel returns null when there is no voice. Call buttons are disabled (busy), Join voice is disabled (call !== null), and selectChannel will not join. You cannot end the call (the peer hears silence) until the peer hangs up. The same happens on the caller side if attach fails in reconcile.
confirmed.fix: Primary fix is in the backend. In Media::call_accept, when attach_locked fails after Net accepted, call core.net.call_hangup().await, as voice_join already cleans up at session.rs:588-590. In reconcile's pending-call attach (session.rs:236), on Err, drop the lock and hang up (or spawn a hangup). UI fallback: in CallPanel, render a minimal panel with 'Hang up' (leaveVoice) whenever `!voice && call && call.state !== 'ringing-in'`, which covers both ringing-out and active.
confirmed.verify: The UI path is real. After Net call_accept activates the call (hub.rs:594-595), an attach_locked failure leaves the call Active with nothing attached. call-updated sets s.call to active and voice stays null. CallPanel returns null (line 41), the call buttons are busy, Join voice is disabled (VoiceView.tsx:231) and selectChannel will not join, so nothing in the UI can end the call. The trigger is rare, though. AudioEngine::new fails only if the audio thread cannot be spawned, and per notes-tincan-audio.md device problems never fail start_call, so this needs an exotic engine failure.

confirmed.title: The download command's result can overwrite a newer transfer-updated, leaving an attachment card stuck
confirmed.scenario: cmd_download starts files.download and returns transfer_dto (queued or downloading). A small file from a LAN peer can finish, and its 'complete' transfer-updated reach the UI, before the command response does. `.then(t => transferStore.set(hash, t))` then replaces 'complete' with the older 'queued' state. No further event comes for that hash, and ensureTransfer skips known hashes, so the card shows a disabled 'Queued' button (or a frozen percentage) until restart.
confirmed.fix: `const before = transferStore.get(hash); run(invoke('download', { hash }).then((t) => { if (transferStore.get(hash) === before) transferStore.set(hash, t); }));` As a backstop, never replace a 'complete' state with a non-complete one.
confirmed.verify: Real, and more plausible than described. cmd_download returns transfer_dto right after files.download spawns the task (transfers.rs:355-357). With no online holder, the task in download.rs run() does only local store work (set_tag, local check) and then emits Unavailable within milliseconds. A 'queued' response delivered after that event overwrites it, and the card shows a disabled 'Queued' button until a holder appears and new events arrive. If a small file completes inside that window, the card is stuck until restart, because no later event comes and ensureTransfer skips known hashes. ensureTransfer (actions.ts:606) already guards the same race and downloadFile does not.

confirmed.title: Closing Settings or switching tabs within 250 ms of moving a volume slider drops the change
confirmed.scenario: You drag Input volume to 150% and click Done (or press Escape, or switch tabs) within 250 ms. The unmount cleanup clears the pending debounce timer, so onCommit never runs and settings_set is never sent. The slider showed 150%, but the saved value is still the old one, as you see when you reopen Settings.
confirmed.fix: Keep `latest` and `onCommit` in refs updated on each change and render. In the unmount cleanup: `if (timer.current) { clearTimeout(timer.current); timer.current = null; commitRef.current(latestRef.current); }`. saveSettings is store-level, so committing after unmount is safe.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. VolumeSlider's unmount cleanup (SettingsDialog.tsx:182-184) clears the pending 250 ms timer without committing. Closing the dialog or switching tabs (both unmount the slider) within 250 ms of the last change, for example keyboard arrows then Escape, drops the value, and reopening shows the old one.

confirmed.title: The auto-download menu offers 50 MB and 100 MB, but the backend silently clamps to 25 MB
confirmed.scenario: You pick 'Up to 50 MB'. settings::normalize clamps autoFetchLimit to MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES (25 MiB), and patch({ settings: saved }) snaps the select back to 'Up to 25 MB' without any message. Attachments are capped at 25 MiB anyway, so the larger options can never apply.
confirmed.fix: `const FETCH_LIMITS = [0, 5 * MB, 10 * MB, 25 * MB];`
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. settings.rs:65 clamps auto_fetch_limit to MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES (25 * 1024 * 1024), the UI's MB is 1024 * 1024, and notes-tincan-app.md:176 documents the clamp. Picking 50 MB or 100 MB is saved as 25 MiB, and the select snaps back with no message.

confirmed.title: After a restart the per-user volume slider shows 100% while a saved volume is applied
confirmed.scenario: You set Alex to 30%. set_user_volume saves it in kv app/user_volumes, and load_volumes applies it after a restart. The UI's `volumes` map is module memory only, so after a restart the popover shows 100%. A small drag then jumps Alex from 30% to about 100%.
confirmed.fix: Add `volume: number` (0..2) to VoiceParticipant in dto.rs, types.ts and docs/api.md, filled from st.volumes (default 1.0) in voice_dto. Seed VolumePopover with `volumes.get(p.userId) ?? p.volume`.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. set_user_volume persists to kv (session.rs save_volumes) and load_volumes/apply_volumes reapply it after a restart. VoiceView's `volumes` map is module memory only, and VoiceParticipant has no volume field, so after a restart the popover starts at 100% while 30% is applied. Any small adjustment jumps the volume to about 100%.

confirmed.title: A lag snapshot does not resync the keyed transfer and speaking stores
confirmed.scenario: The shell's UI forwarder lags and drops events, then sends a snapshot. Dropped events can include a final transfer-updated (complete) and the speaking:false that refresh_room or detach emits for someone who left your room while talking. applySnapshot reseeds speaking only for snap.voice participants and never touches transferStore, and ensureTransfer skips known hashes. Result: attachment cards stay at 'downloading X%' with no Open button, and avatars of people who left keep the speaking ring in the sidebar and member list.
confirmed.fix: Add `keys()` to KeyedStore. In applySnapshot when wasReady, run invoke('transfer', { hash }) for every transferStore entry whose state is not 'complete', and set the result only if the entry did not change while the request was in flight. Leave speaking as is.
confirmed.verify: Only the transfer half holds. The speaking half is already handled: applySnapshot calls loadServer for every server (actions.ts:315), and loadServer writes speakingStore for every member (actions.ts:120). cmd_members returns all server members with speaking = media.is_speaking(u) (views.rs:297), so stale rings are cleared. Nothing reseeds transferStore, though: remounted Attachment cards call ensureTransfer, which skips known hashes, so a dropped final transfer-updated leaves the card at 'Queued' or 'X%' until restart. The trigger, a lag in the shell forwarder with a 1024-event buffer and non-blocking emit, is very rare.

confirmed.title: Message caches of loaded conversations grow without limit for the whole session
confirmed.scenario: Every conversation you have opened keeps an entry in s.messages. Every later message-added for it is appended (list = [...c.list, m]), even when it is not on screen, and nothing evicts entries except a snapshot. With the app left open for days in busy servers, memory grows with every message received in any channel you have ever opened.
confirmed.fix: In putMessage, when the message is not for the conversation on screen and c.list.length >= 300, delete s.messages[key] instead of appending. ensureMessages reloads it on the next open. For the conversation on screen, optionally trim the oldest entries beyond a cap when stick is true, and set the cursor to the new oldest entry's cursor.
confirmed.verify: Accurate. putMessage appends to every loaded conversation's list and nothing evicts off-screen entries except a snapshot. In normal use the growth is small (about 1 KB per message received in conversations you opened), and snapshots after reconnect catch-ups reset it, so it matters only for sessions left open for days in very busy servers. buildRows also re-walks the whole list for the open conversation on every message.

confirmed.title: open_file runs any peer-named file (exe, hta, js, lnk, scr) through explorer.exe with no allowlist, no Mark-of-the-Web and no confirmation
confirmed.scenario:
Messages keep the peer's attachment name and declared mime (views.rs:325). safe_file_name keeps the extension (shell.rs:84-101). cmd_open_file exports the blob and calls open_with_default_app, which runs `explorer.exe <path>` (shell.rs:127-134). Nothing checks the extension, and the export gets no Zone.Identifier stream, so SmartScreen, Attachment Manager and Office Protected View never fire. Auto-fetch defaults to 25 MB (settings.rs:22, transfers.rs:267), so the file is already complete when the message shows.

Path (a): a peer posts name "Invoice.pdf" + 60 x U+00A0 + ".exe" with mime "application/pdf". The card shows the PDF icon (Attachment.tsx:138) and "Invoice.pdf ...". `.truncate` hides the rest, and NBSP is not collapsed. One click on Open (Attachment.tsx:69) runs the exe silently.

Path (b): a peer posts name "cat.hta" with mime "image/gif". The bytes are a valid GIF followed by `<script>new ActiveXObject('WScript.Shell').Run(...)</script>`. serve_mime sniffs GIF, so the inline preview renders (Attachment.tsx:129-130). The name appears only in a hover tooltip. Clicking the picture to enlarge it calls openFile (Attachment.tsx:115), and mshta runs the script with the user's rights. mshta parses HTML anywhere in the file.
confirmed.fix: 1. In cmd_open_file, take the lowercased extension of the final export `path` (after safe_file_name and unique_path, never the peer's name). Launch it only if it is on an inert allowlist: png jpg jpeg gif webp bmp mp3 wav ogg flac m4a mp4 webm mov txt pdf. For anything else, reveal the file instead. Use `Command::new("explorer.exe").raw_arg(format!("/select,\"{}\"", path.display()))`: the normal .arg() quoting makes "/select,<path with spaces>" one quoted token, which explorer misparses. 2. After files.export succeeds, write `<path>:Zone.Identifier` = "[ZoneTransfer]\r\nZoneId=3\r\n" on every export, so SmartScreen, Attachment Manager and Protected View apply to allowlisted types and to later double-clicks in Explorer. 3. In message_dto, build the DTO mime from shell::mime_for_name(&safe_file_name(&a.name)) instead of the peer's a.mime. The icon and the image-preview decision (Attachment.tsx:129) then match what open_file will launch, so a "cat.hta" never renders as a clickable picture.
confirmed.verify: I followed the code end to end and the path holds. message_dto (views.rs:325) sends the peer's a.name and a.mime unchanged. Attachment.tsx:69 (Open) and :115 (clicking the image preview) both call openFile(a.hash, a.name). dispatch.rs:264 calls cmd_open_file, which exports to downloadDir/safe_file_name(name) (transfers.rs:397). safe_file_name keeps any extension (shell.rs:84-101), and transfers.rs:412 then runs `explorer.exe <path>` (shell.rs:133). Nothing checks the extension, writes Zone.Identifier or asks for confirmation (I grepped for Zone.Identifier and an allowlist; neither exists). validate_message (tincan-core state.rs:829) only checks the length of attachment names, so NBSP padding is allowed. Auto-fetch defaults to 25 MiB (settings.rs:22), so the blob is already complete and Open shows at once. Path (a) is the solid case: name "Invoice.pdf" + NBSPs + ".exe" with mime application/pdf. The card shows the text icon (FileIcon uses the peer's mime) and a truncated "Invoice.pdf ...". One click and explorer runs the exe. With no MOTW, SmartScreen and Attachment Manager never check it. A plain "x.exe", .lnk, .js, .vbs, .bat or .hta also runs on one click. Path (b) holds as far as the code goes: serve_mime sniffs GIF89a, so the preview renders, and clicking it exports "cat.hta" and launches it. That mshta runs a script placed after GIF bytes is a known polyglot technique, but I could not confirm it from the code, so it is unverified. The verdict rests on path (a).

confirmed.title: Any DM peer or member of any shared server can download every blob I hold, including other people's private DM attachments
confirmed.scenario:
The blob access policy only checks the user: `Arc::new(move |u| check.read().contains(u))` (app.rs:158). The provider applies it once per connection (tincan-files provider.rs:60) and serves any hash after that.

The allowed set is the union of all members of all my servers plus every DM peer (update_policy, app.rs:269). on_dm_opened adds any peer whose incoming DM created a conversation (commands.rs:293). Incoming DMs are accepted from anyone who knows my user id (dm.rs:435-449), and server member lists show user ids.

The app also puts every complete hash, across all conversations and kinds, into the global Have list: net.set_have(files.complete_hashes()) at app.rs:178, have_add at pump.rs:332, and clips.rs:229/519. tincan-net returns that full list in the DmHello reply (dm.rs:431) and in every Have broadcast (dm.rs:244), and also gives it to every server host.

Attack: Mallory, a co-member of any server (or anyone with my contact code), opens a DM connection. She gets my full hash list in the hello reply, is added to `allowed`, then connects with the files ALPN and fetches each hash. That includes Alice's private DM attachments and files from servers Mallory never joined. Whoever becomes host of a shared server (hosting is not a privilege) also receives every member's Have list and can do the same.
confirmed.fix: 1. Authorise per (peer, hash). In tincan-files, set get/get_many to RequestMode::Intercept, and observe to Intercept as well, so possession cannot be probed. iroh-blobs 0.105 RequestReceived carries connection_id and the request but no endpoint id (events.rs:672-678). So record connection_id -> UserId at ClientConnected, drop it at ConnectionClosed, and call a new `AccessPolicy::allow(peer, hash)` for each requested hash. 2. In the app, allow (peer, H) only when H is a library clip and the peer shares a server with me, or some conversation that references H includes the peer: a current member of that server, or that DM's peer. This needs a persistent hash -> set-of-conversations index filled at message ingest. Core::atts cannot serve: it keeps only the first conversation (SECURITY-8), lives in memory, and is cleared at 50k entries. Persisted app/att records exist only for downloads and sends. 3. Until tincan-net has per-conversation Have lists, stop putting DM-only attachment hashes into set_have/have_add (app.rs:178, pump.rs:332, clips.rs:229/519). DM who_has never uses Have (net.rs:432-434). Tell the tincan-net owner that DmHello and DM Have deltas should not carry the global have list, and that each server's host should only get the hashes referenced in that server.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. The policy is per user only: app.rs:158 `check.read().contains(u)`. tincan-files checks it once, in ClientConnected (provider.rs:58-73). EVENT_MASK has get/get_many: RequestMode::None (provider.rs:33-34), so an allowed peer is then served any hash in the store. `allowed` is every member of every server plus every DM peer (update_policy, app.rs:269-282), and on_dm_opened adds any DM peer (commands.rs:293). Incoming DMs have no gate at all: DmProto::accept (proto.rs:77-88) leads to accept_incoming (dm.rs:435), which checks only that conv == ConvId::dm(me, peer). open_conv then creates the replica and emits DmOpened (dm.rs:373-374), and pump.rs:290-292 calls on_dm_opened. The reply to that hello is dm_hello(), which carries net.have_list() (dm.rs:431, 450), i.e. every hash I hold. The app feeds that global list everything: set_have(files.complete_hashes()) at app.rs:178 and clips.rs:229/519, and have_add at pump.rs:332, DM attachments included. Servers' hosts get the same list in Hello (net.rs:324, session/mod.rs:1180), and every DM link gets each Have delta (dm.rs:244). So anyone who knows my user id (any co-member sees it in member DTOs; a contact code gives it too) dials tincan/dm/1, receives my full hash list, is added to `allowed`, then fetches every blob over the files ALPN. That includes other people's private DM attachments and files from servers they never joined. The fix sits in the app (policy and what it announces) and in tincan-files, not in tincan-net's own logic.

confirmed.title: Bidi-override and zero-width characters in peer file names and display names are kept, so extensions and nearby UI text can be spoofed
confirmed.scenario:
Rust's char::is_control matches only category Cc. So U+202E (RLO), U+2066-2069, U+200B-200F and U+FEFF pass tincan-core's name checks (state.rs:805). Attachment names get no character check at all (state.rs:829). They also pass clips::remote_name (clips.rs:154) and safe_file_name (shell.rs:88). views.rs sends names to the UI unchanged, and the UI renders them without isolation.

Example 1: a peer sends attachment "invoice‮fdp.exe". The file card (Attachment.tsx:141) and its tooltip show "invoiceexe.pdf". The exported file keeps the RLO, so the download folder in Explorer shows the same fake name. Open then runs the exe (SECURITY-1).

Example 2: a display name ending in U+202E reverses the text after it. `${names[0]} is typing` (Composer.tsx:131) and `${call.name} is calling` (IncomingCallDialog.tsx) render backwards.

Example 3: "Bob​" renders exactly like "Bob".
confirmed.fix: 1. In safe_file_name, map U+061C, U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2060-U+2069 and U+FEFF to '_' together with control characters. This is the part that protects file names. 2. In views.rs DTOs for peer display, server and channel names, and in clips::remote_name, strip only the bidi embedding, override and isolate controls: U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 (plus U+061C). Do not strip U+200C/U+200D: they are needed for emoji ZWJ sequences and Persian/Indic text. 3. In the UI, wrap interpolated names in <bdi> or give the name classes `unicode-bidi: isolate`. This only stops an override leaking into the text around it. The name itself still renders reversed, so steps 1-2 are the real protection.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. char::is_control matches only general category Cc. So U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069, U+200B-200F and U+FEFF (all Cf) pass every filter: check_name for display, server and channel names (tincan-core state.rs:805), clips::remote_name (clips.rs:154), and safe_file_name (shell.rs:88). validate_message (state.rs:829) applies no character rule to attachment names at all. views.rs passes names through unchanged (message_dto :325, author_name :198-206, user_name :181-195, members :289). The UI has no bidi isolation anywhere (a grep for unicode-bidi, <bdi> and dir=auto finds nothing). So "invoice<U+202E>fdp.exe" renders as "invoiceexe.pdf" on the file card (Attachment.tsx:141), in its title tooltip, and in the Downloads folder listing, because the export keeps the RLO. The tooltip fooling a careful user is what makes this worse than the NBSP trick. Today it feeds SECURITY-1's one-click execution. After that fix, the exported file still carries a misleading name in Explorer. An override in a display name also flips the template text after it (Composer.tsx:131, IncomingCallDialog.tsx:11). That part is cosmetic.

confirmed.title: Peer display names are not unique and nothing in the UI tells two users apart, so impersonating a contact is trivial
confirmed.scenario:
author_name, user_name and members (views.rs:181-206, 278) return whatever name the peer published. The UI shows a peer only by that name plus an avatar colour, hashIndex(userId, 8) (format.ts:70, common.tsx). That is one of 8 colours, so a matching key takes a few tries to generate. No screen shows another user's id (only my own userCode appears, in SettingsDialog).
