Attack: Mallory joins a server Bob is in, sets her name to "Bob" and picks a key whose colour matches his. Her messages and member row look identical to Bob's. She then DMs the victim. user_name takes the server name, so the DM sidebar shows two identical "Bob" rows. She sends the disguised file from SECURITY-1 as "Bob".
confirmed.fix: Keep it minimal. Always show short_name(user) (views.rs:92), the first 8 z32 characters, as secondary text in the DM chat header (ChatView DmChat), the member row menu and the incoming-call dialog. Expose it either as a field the UI already has (userId) or as a ready-made `shortId` in the DTOs. Optionally, also append " · <shortId>" to the name when two current members of a view, or two DM summaries, share a case-insensitive name. Do not rely on NFKC or case-folding to catch impersonation: they do not fold Cyrillic or Greek homoglyphs, so always showing the id is the part that works.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. Display names are unique nowhere: tincan-core applies only check_name to Profile (state.rs:669, 710), with no collision rule. author_name, user_name and members return the published name as is (views.rs:181-206, 289). No UI surface shows another user's id: I grepped components, dialogs and screens, and the only user id displayed is my own userCode in SettingsDialog. The only other cue is the avatar colour, hashIndex(userId, 8), and a matching colour takes about 8 key generations. So Mallory, as a co-member, sets her name to "Bob" and is indistinguishable in messages and the member list. user_name takes a server-sourced name for DMs (views.rs:188), so her DM shows up as a second identical "Bob" row. This is plausible in any server with an untrusted member and is undetectable in the app.

confirmed.title: safe_file_name cuts the whole name at 200 characters, which can drop the real extension and expose an earlier .exe
confirmed.scenario:
`out.chars().take(200)` runs after the trailing-dot strip and keeps the start of the name. Peer names can be up to 255 characters (state.rs:94).

A name "Holiday" + 189 x U+00A0 + ".exe" + ".jpg" (204 characters, mime image/jpeg) shows an image icon. Its tooltip and alt text end in ".jpg". It is exported as "Holiday<NBSP...>.exe", and open_file launches the exe.

This also bypasses any extension allowlist that checks the peer's name rather than the final path.
confirmed.fix: Truncate the stem, not the whole name. After sanitising, split off the last extension when it is 1-16 characters with no spaces, cut the stem so `stem + "." + ext` is at most 200 characters, then strip trailing dots and spaces from the stem again. If the name is empty, use "file". Re-run the reserved-name check on the result. Any open-time allowlist (SECURITY-1) must read the extension of the final path.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. safe_file_name ends with `out.chars().take(200)` (shell.rs:101), which keeps the start of the name, and peer attachment names may be up to 255 characters (state.rs:94, 829). "Holiday" + 189 NBSP + ".exe" + ".jpg" is 204 characters and comes out as "Holiday.exe". With mime image/jpeg and exe bytes, serve_mime serves image/jpeg (the hint is a safe inline type), the fails, and onFail drops to the file card with the image icon. The title tooltip and alt text end in ".jpg", and Open exports and launches the .exe (transfers.rs:397, 412). This is mostly an amplifier for SECURITY-1: it fools even a user who hovers, and it defeats any allowlist that checks the peer's name. Once SECURITY-1's check uses the final path, what remains is a saved file whose extension differs from the one shown (MOTW then applies). Hence low.

confirmed.title: Reject text from a host is shown to the user unchanged as Tincan's own error message
confirmed.scenario:
net_err maps every NetError other than Core and Endpoint with `other => other.to_string()`. NetError::Rejected carries the peer's Reject reason: reject_inflight in session/member.rs:221 for publishes, and BadInvite on join at net.rs:708. Frames can be up to 1 MB.

Attack: Mallory becomes host of a shared server, or owns a server whose invite the victim accepts. She rejects every publish with "Tincan blocked this message. Your client is out of date: install the security update from tincan-update[.]example and restart." The Composer shows that text as the app's error (Composer.tsx setError(errorText(err))). Toasts do the same through run(). A multi-KB reason fills the screen.
confirmed.fix: In net_err, map NetError::Rejected coming from publish refusals to a fixed sentence, for example "The host refused this message.". If the reason is kept, prefix it with "The host says: ", remove Cc/Cf characters, and cap it at about 200 characters. Ask tincan-net for a separate variant (for example RejectedByPeer(String)) so local Rejected texts such as "This invite has expired." and the version message stay verbatim.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. on_ack (session/member.rs:178) takes `reason` straight from the host's Ack frame. For a non-gap refusal, reject_inflight (member.rs:213-223) wraps it as NetError::Rejected(capitalize(reason)), with no length cap or character filtering; the only bound is MAX_FRAME, 1 MiB (tincan-core wire.rs:17). Join BadInvite does the same at net.rs:708. net_err (app.rs:397-409) maps every variant other than Core and Endpoint with `other.to_string()`, so the host's text becomes the command error for send_message, edit, delete, server updates and the rest (commands.rs:117, 142, 158, 168, 240, 260). errorText (client.ts:54-66) passes unknown strings through, and Composer.tsx:55/74 shows them as Tincan's own error. React escapes the text, so there is no injection. But any member who becomes host (hosting is not a privilege) can show arbitrary phishing text, up to about 1 MB, in the app's own error area.

confirmed.title: The attachment index keeps the first (conv, author) seen for each hash, so a peer who posts a hash first can block that file's real download
confirmed.scenario:
index_attachments uses `entry(a.hash).or_insert_with(...)`, so the first message seen with hash H fixes where H is fetched from. start_download persists that record (transfers.rs:176, app/att/<hash>).

Attack: Mallory knows H (for example from the leaked Have list, SECURITY-2) and posts H to the victim before the victim's app indexes Alice's real message. The victim's auto-fetch asks only Mallory's conversation, and Mallory never serves the file, so the download parks. Alice's message is then skipped: a transfer already exists and H is in `seen`. Download and Requery both use att_ref(H), which is Mallory's entry, so Alice's server and holders are never asked. The file stays unavailable, and after a restart too.
confirmed.fix: Keep a set of (conv, author) origins per hash, both in Core::atts and in the persisted app/att record, adding an origin for every message seen instead of keeping only the first. In start_download, Requery and Peers, call who_has for each origin conversation that is still loaded, merge and dedupe the holders, and build providers with every origin author. A smaller alternative is to pass the message's convId from the UI to `download`/`transfer` and add that origin before querying.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. index_attachments uses `entry(a.hash).or_insert_with(..)` (views.rs:343-346), so the first (conv, author) seen for a hash wins. Mallory's message with H in a DM is indexed and auto-fetched, and start_download persists that AttRef (transfers.rs:233). who_has on the DM returns only Mallory (net.rs:432-434), so if she does not serve the file the transfer parks. Alice's later message with H in a server is not re-indexed. auto_fetch skips it because files.transfer(H) is Some (transfers.rs:269), and the worker skips it because H is already in `seen` (transfers.rs:100). cmd_download (transfers.rs:352-355), Requery (:121-127) and requery_parked all use att_ref(H), so only Mallory's DM is asked again and the file stays unavailable while Alice's server holders are never queried. The same thing happens without an attacker when one file is posted in two conversations and the first one seen has no online holders. Whether it survives a restart depends on order: att_ref checks memory first and reads the persisted record only on a miss. It sticks only if something, such as a Resume at first connection, looks H up before Alice's message is indexed. Low: an attacker needs H before the victim sees Alice's message, and the harmless trigger is narrow.

confirmed.title: Auto-fetch trusts the size a peer declares and never checks the real blob size, so a member can make every client download an unbounded blob
confirmed.scenario: auto_fetch (transfers.rs:266-270) queues any attachment whose declared `a.size <= autoFetchLimit` (25 MiB by default). That size comes from the peer's message, and validate_message (tincan-core state.rs:818-836) only checks names and MIME types. tincan-files has no size cap: the download learns the real total from the first verified chunk (download.rs:301-308) and keeps going until the blob is complete. on_transfer (transfers.rs:287-318) never compares info.total with the declared size or with MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES. The clip path does (clips.rs:450-464), the attachment path does not. Attack: a member posts Attachment{size:1000, hash:H}, where H is a 200 GB blob they serve. Every online member, and every later joiner through history sync, auto-downloads all 200 GB. The data is tagged att-<hex>, so hourly GC never frees it, and disks fill. Each victim that completes the blob calls have_add (pump.rs:330-333) and starts serving it, which amplifies the load past the attacker's own uplink. Growth: the attacker's upload rate per victim, then the victims' combined rate, until the disk is full.
confirmed.fix: Do not refuse when the total differs from AttRef.size. The index is first-writer-wins (views.rs:344 or_insert_with), so a member could pre-post a known hash with a wrong size and make legitimate downloads get refused. Cap on absolute limits instead. Sturdiest fix: give Files::download/request a max_size, and enforce it in download.rs attempt() where the size is learned (303-308). If size > max: fail the request, drop its kind tag and emit Failed. The app passes min(auto_fetch_limit, MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES) for Auto and MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES for cmd_download and Resume. As an app-side backstop, check in on_transfer for Attachment kind: if info.total > MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES, or the download was auto-started and total > auto_fetch_limit, then call files.cancel, spawn remove_kind(hash, Attachment), set the download record to failed, and persist a refused marker (kv). auto_fetch, cmd_download and the Resume branch check that marker, so a restart's partial_downloads does not refetch it.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed end to end. auto_fetch (transfers.rs:266-270) gates on the peer-declared a.size. validate_message (core state.rs:818-836) never checks size. tincan-files has no size limit: grep finds only MAX_ACTIVE_DOWNLOADS and the upload limiter, and download.rs:301-308 only records the real total. on_transfer (transfers.rs:287-318) and cmd_download never compare info.total with MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES; only the clip path does (clips.rs:450-464). The pump calls auto_fetch for every history message, bulk included (pump.rs:232), so later joiners are hit too. Blobs are tagged att-, and nothing in the app ever calls remove/remove_kind for attachments, so GC never frees them. pump.rs:330-333 calls have_add on completion, so victims start serving the blob, which amplifies the attack. The only cap is read_to_bytes(MAX) in file_for_url, which limits serving to the webview, not the download. A modified client posts {size:1000, hash:H of a multi-GB blob}, and every member's disk fills.

confirmed.title: Every roster update redials offline providers for every parked download and floods the shared fetch queue
confirmed.scenario: pump.rs:269-273 sets rosters_changed on every RosterUpdated from any server. flush then calls requery_parked (transfers.rs:278-284), which try_sends one Requery per Unavailable hash. The 10 s per-hash throttle (transfers.rs:114-121) runs only after dequeue. For each requery the worker makes one who_has round trip (up to 3 s), then calls providers() (207-229). providers() always appends the author even when the author is offline, so add_providers is never skipped. tincan-files' merge (download.rs:80-95) then marks every provider that already failed as pending again. The download wakes, takes one of the 3 download slots, dials the offline peer (the 4 s connect timeout) and parks again. Along the way it emits Queued, Downloading and Unavailable; each state change costs a SQLite get plus upsert (transfers.rs:297-309) and a transfer-updated UI event. Wake frequency: the host rebroadcasts the roster when any member's RTT crosses a 25 ms bucket at its 2 s tick (session/host.rs:985-994), and on every mute, voice or share change. So in an active server, each parked download redials dead peers about every 10 s for as long as they stay offline. Example: 50 images were posted while I was away, and everyone who holds them is now offline. That gives 50 dead dials every 10 s. With more than about 7 parked downloads (3 slots × 10 s / 4 s) the slots are always busy, so a Download the user clicks on an available file waits in the semaphore queue behind them. With a few hundred parked hashes, each roster update enqueues hundreds of items and fills the 1024 queue, so Auto and Peers try_sends are dropped. The retain call in the worker also makes each wave O(P²).
confirmed.fix: Keep the current trigger. Gating it on 'someone new came online' would regress holder discovery: an already-online member who completes the blob never changes the roster. (1) Throttle before enqueue: keep a requeried-at map in Core and have requery_parked skip hashes requeried less than REQUERY_EVERY ago. (2) In the Requery branch, add only providers with net.peer_online(u). This drops the offline author that providers() appends. Skip add_providers when none are left, so a parked download never wakes just to dial dead peers. (3) Also requery on DmLinkUp. Today a DM-only profile never gets RosterUpdated, so parked DM attachments are never retried when the contact reconnects.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. Every RosterUpdated sets rosters_changed (pump.rs:269-273), and flush calls requery_parked, which try_sends one Requery per Unavailable hash with no throttle before enqueue (transfers.rs:278-284). The 10 s throttle only applies after dequeue (114-121). providers() always appends the author, even offline, unless the author is me (225-227), so add_providers is never skipped. merge() re-marks providers that already failed as pending (download.rs:80-95). The download goes Queued, takes a FIFO slot (3 slots, files.rs:50) and dials the offline author. The iroh-util pool has no negative caching, the 4 s CONNECT_TIMEOUT applies, and presets::N0 discovery returns a stale relay, so the dial times out instead of failing fast. The host re-marks the roster when any member's RTT crosses a 25 ms bucket at its tick (host.rs:985-994). With more than about 7 parked hashes the slots stay busy with dead dials, so a Download the user clicks waits behind them for tens of seconds. Parked downloads are common, because auto-fetch parks every history attachment whose author is offline. The O(P^2) retain part is negligible. Each wave also does Requery who_has round trips that delay Auto and Peers.

confirmed.title: Joining a server with a large history fills the 1024 fetch queue with the oldest attachments, drops the newest for good, and starves the UI's holder lookups
confirmed.scenario: The pump calls auto_fetch for every history message, bulk or not (pump.rs:232). History arrives per author in ascending seq (notes-tincan-net.md:60), at thousands of events per second. The single worker handles one Auto per who_has round trip (member to host, up to the 3 s budget) plus 2 SQLite writes (transfers.rs:233-245). The queue (FETCH_QUEUE 1024, app.rs:32) therefore fills within the first ~1024 attachments in stream order. Every later try_send fails with only a debug log (270-272). Nothing rescans: auto-fetch fires only on arrival, and events lost to a lag (pump.rs:182) are lost too. Example: a server with 3000 attachments. The newcomer prefetches roughly the 1000 that come first in stream order, which are the oldest posts of the first authors, and never prefetches the newest ~2000. The newest are the ones shown first, and the most likely to lose their holders. The UI's Peers lookups (cmd_transfer, 338-344) share the same queue. While it is full they are dropped, and the UI asks `transfer` only once per hash (actions.ts:601-609), so cards keep showing 'No one online has it'. While it is not full they wait behind up to 1024 Autos: at least about 50 s at a 50 ms RTT, up to about 51 minutes at the 3 s budget. resume_downloads (app.rs:333-337) takes its list and then try_sends into the same queue, so a partial download beyond capacity is never resumed.
confirmed.fix: Give Peers (and Requery) their own small channel, or drain it first in the worker with a biased select over two receivers. For Auto, skip per-message enqueue while the conversation is in bulk. At bulk end (pump on_timer), read the newest N attachment messages of that conversation from storage and enqueue them newest first. Alternatively, make the Auto queue a bounded deque that drops the oldest entries and pops the newest first. In resume_downloads, put the items whose try_send failed back into core.resume instead of dropping them.
confirmed.verify: The core mechanism holds. auto_fetch runs for every history message (pump.rs:232). History streams per author in ascending seq (notes-tincan-net.md sync). The single worker awaits a who_has round trip per Auto (start_download, transfers.rs:244). So the 1024 queue (app.rs:32) fills with the earliest items in stream order, and the newest attachments are dropped with only a debug log. Peers lookups (cmd_transfer 338-344) share the queue: they are dropped when it is full and wait behind up to 1024 Autos when it is not. The UI asks `transfer` only once per hash (actions.ts:601-609), so the holder count on visible cards stays stale. Two claims are overstated. First, 'No one online has it' appears only when the author is offline, because online_holders counts an online author without a lookup (transfers.rs:194-203). Second, partials dropped by resume_downloads are not lost for good: partial_downloads re-lists them at the next start. Also, the queue-full drop is a deliberate, logged fallback, and Download still works on click, because cmd_download calls who_has directly. The real defect is a priority inversion: the oldest items are kept and the newest dropped, and Peers starve behind Autos. That is minor wrong behaviour, not a blocked task.

confirmed.title: The UI clip list grows without bound from peers' sound-played announcements
confirmed.scenario: The sound-played handler (actions.ts:399-402) appends any clip whose hash is not yet in s.clips. The backend caps heard clips at 50 (clips.rs:32, 62-68), but the UI list only shrinks on clips-updated. The backend sends that on add, remove, rename, pull progress and detach, never from on_sound. A member in my voice room can send Ctl::SoundPlayed with a fresh random hash each time. The SFU forwards it with no rate limit (net media/sfu.rs:506-520), and on_sound only checks size and duration (clips.rs:375-395). Each announcement adds one Clip object (~300 B) plus an O(n) `some` and an O(n) array copy, so the total cost is quadratic. The Soundboard renders one HeardTile per entry and runs nameOf, which scans every member list, for each tile. At 50 announcements per second that is 180k entries per hour. Each new event then costs about 360k operations, and an open soundboard renders 180k tiles. This lasts until I leave voice.
confirmed.fix: In the sound-played handler, after appending, keep the owned clips plus only the newest 50 non-owned ones (matching MAX_HEARD). In on_sound, rate-limit per (conv, by): for example, ignore more than 2 announcements per second, or more than 1 per clip duration, per user.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. The sound-played handler (actions.ts:399-402) appends any clip whose hash is unknown. The backend caps heard clips at 50 (clips.rs:32, 62-68), but on_sound (375-396) never emits clips-updated; that comes only from fetch, clip transfers, add/remove/rename and detach. A snapshot does not reset s.clips (applySnapshot loads clips only when !wasReady). The SFU forwards Ctl::SoundPlayed from any room member with no rate limit (net sfu.rs:506-520), and on_sound only checks size and duration. A malicious member in my voice room who sends random hashes grows the UI list without bound, with O(n) some plus a copy per event. Soundboard.tsx renders a HeardTile per non-owned clip and runs nameOf for each, so an open soundboard becomes unusable. This lasts until I leave voice.

confirmed.title: Message caches of conversations that are off screen grow forever with live traffic, and reopening one renders all of it
confirmed.scenario: putMessage (actions.ts:187-211) appends every message-added to any conversation that was ever loaded (`if (!c) return` only skips conversations never visited). state.messages is cleared only by a snapshot (actions.ts:307), and snapshots come only from bulk ends, set_name, join or leave, or a lag. A busy channel visited once keeps growing while the user is elsewhere. Each message is about 0.5-1 KB of JS (64-char ids, z32 author, text up to 4000 chars). Each append also costs an O(n) findIndex plus an O(n) slice. When the user returns, MessageList builds and renders every row (no windowing, MessageList.tsx:148, 245). Growth: the summed message rate of every visited conversation. At 1 message per 10 s in each of 5 visited channels that is about 43k messages, roughly 20-40 MB of heap, per day, and tens of thousands of DOM nodes on revisit.
confirmed.fix: In putMessage, when the message's conversation is not the one in view (the same check markSeen uses), delete s.messages[key] instead of appending, so the next view reloads its newest page. Alternatively, cap each cached list (for example the newest 200 plus the loaded older pages) and drop the caches of conversations left in afterViewChange.
confirmed.verify: The path holds. putMessage (actions.ts:187-211) appends to any conversation already loaded. store.ts has no other pruning; messages are reset only by applySnapshot when wasReady (actions.ts:307). MessageList renders every row with no windowing. In practice, though, growth is bounded more than the finding says. Every bulk end with suppressed messages emits a snapshot that wipes all caches (pump.rs:349-351), and so do join, leave, set_name and UI lag. Catch-ups after sleep or a reconnect trigger bulk. Growth is the live traffic of visited conversations between such events. At this app's small-group scale that is a few MB per day and a slow re-render on revisit, not a serious leak, except on an always-on, never-disconnected desktop in a very busy server.

confirmed.title: Every Members change does a full Net::conv_state clone (the message index included), per event and peer-triggerable
confirmed.scenario: On Change::Members outside bulk, the pump invalidates the view and calls core.update_policy() at once, with no debounce (pump.rs:256-265). update_policy calls view() for every conversation (app.rs:269-282), and view() rebuilds the invalidated one through net.conv_state (views.rs:162). That clones the whole ConvState under the replica mutex (net.rs:380): message_authors has one entry per message ever (~65 B per hashbrown slot, about 8.5 MB at 100k messages), plus deleted, heads, invites and members. Body::Profile yields Change::Members whenever ev.hlc >= name_hlc, even if the name is unchanged (tincan-core state.rs:710-714). Bulk detection counts only Message events (pump.rs:197, 220), so a member who publishes Profile events in a loop makes every member do one O(history) clone per event. At 10 per second on a 100k-message server that is about 85 MB/s of alloc plus memcpy, and net's event application stalls on the held replica lock each time. During a bulk sync, each Members event sets policy_dirty, and every 100 ms flush then clones the growing state again (pump.rs:261, 373-376). refresh_dms (app.rs:358-364) also calls view() on server conversations only to learn they are not DMs.
confirmed.fix: Do not simply move Members into the 100 ms debounce. pump.rs:263 needs a newly admitted member allowed at once. Use leading-edge plus coalescing instead: run update_policy immediately if none ran in the last ~100 ms, otherwise set policy_dirty for the flush. In update_policy and refresh_dms, skip conversations that are in bulk (bulk end already sets policy_dirty). In refresh_dms, use storage.convs().is_dm instead of view(). Longer term, add a Net accessor that builds a projection under the lock without cloning message_authors and deleted. That needs a tincan-net API change.
confirmed.verify: The path is real. On Change::Members outside bulk, the pump calls invalidate_view and then update_policy at once (pump.rs:256-265). That rebuilds the view via net.conv_state, which clones the whole ConvState under the replica lock (net.rs:380), message_authors and deleted included. Body::Profile yields Change::Members on every event with hlc >= name_hlc, even when the name is unchanged (state.rs:710-714), and bulk detection counts only Message events (pump.rs:197, 220). So a member spamming Profile events costs every member one O(history) clone per event: a few ms at 100k messages, held under the replica lock. During bulk, each flush with policy_dirty re-clones the growing state, at most every 100 ms. Severity is low: it is CPU amplification only under a malicious member, who can already spam messages, which costs members comparable work and permanent storage. It is not a growing leak, and the bulk-time churn is small next to the sync's own cost.

confirmed.title: A watched screen share keeps being received, copied over IPC and decoded while the window is minimized, with no backpressure when the decoder falls behind
confirmed.scenario: onMessage decodes every access unit unconditionally (ScreenView.tsx:67-91). Only onFrame checks isWindowHidden and throws the decoded frame away (144-147). While the window is minimized, the host keeps forwarding the track because the subscription stays. Rust copies each frame into a new Vec (ui_video_message, session.rs:538) and sends it on the Tauri Channel. Raw bodies of 1 KiB or more are parked in ChannelDataIpcQueue and fetched by JS with an extra IPC invoke per frame (tauri ipc/channel.rs:38, 302-319). WebCodecs then decodes it. Wake rate: the share frame rate, 30-60 per second, plus the share bitrate (Mbps), for as long as the window stays minimized during a call. dec.decode also never checks decodeQueueSize. If the decoder is slower than the stream (software fallback, or a 4K share on a weak GPU), queued chunks and latency grow without bound.
confirmed.fix: Expose a subscribe callback from windowState. On minimize, stop the player: call screen_unwatch and close the decoder. On restore, start it again with screen_watch. The host caches the current GOP (architecture.md:272) and watch() resubscribes (screen.rs:316-321), so playback resumes at once from a keyframe. For backpressure: if dec.decodeQueueSize exceeds a small bound, skip deltas and set needKey until the next keyframe. GOP is 4 s, so that freezes the view for at most about 4 s.
confirmed.verify: Accurate, but it is largely a documented trade-off. architecture.md:61 says the UI pauses rendering, not decoding, on minimize. onMessage decodes every access unit (ScreenView.tsx:67-91), and only onFrame discards frames while hidden (144-147). The subscription stays, so the host keeps forwarding (using its uplink budget), Rust copies each frame into the Tauri Channel, and WebCodecs decodes at the share frame rate for as long as the window is minimized. That is steady, bounded waste (mostly hardware decode plus IPC), not growth. decodeQueueSize is never checked, so latency and memory grow only when the decoder is slower than real time (software fallback on a high-resolution share), which is an edge case.

confirmed.title: Each roster update recomputes members, the server summary and every DM summary, even when nothing they show changed
confirmed.scenario: Every RosterUpdated marks server+members, dms_dirty and rosters_changed (pump.rs:269-273). The host rebroadcasts the roster when any member's RTT crosses a 25 ms bucket at its 2 s tick, and RTT is not part of the Member DTO. So with several online members this can fire about every 2 s per server while idle. Each flush 100 ms later runs members() (views.rs:278-303), which does an O(members × online) find, a sort that allocates two lowercase strings per comparison, and a JSON encode of the whole list for dedup (views.rs:437). It runs server_summary(), which does 2 SQLite queries per visible channel (views.rs:239, 220-221), duplicated when channels refresh in the same pass, plus a roster clone. And it runs refresh_dms() (app.rs:358-364): per DM, a message query, 2 unread queries, a get_contact and a scan of every roster in peer_online. Dedup then suppresses the UI event, not the work. Example: 200 members, 30 channels and 20 DMs gives about 140 SQLite queries plus a 200-entry sort and encode every ~2 s while idle.
confirmed.fix: In the pump, keep a per-server signature of the roster fields the DTOs use (online users, voice, muted, deafened, sharing, host, plus the succession that net already compares). Skip mark, dms_dirty and rosters_changed when it is unchanged. Optionally, compute the channel unread flags once per refresh and reuse them in server_summary.
confirmed.verify: The path is real. Every RosterUpdated marks server+members, dms_dirty and rosters_changed (pump.rs:269-273). The host re-marks the roster on RTT bucket changes at its tick (host.rs:985-994), and RTT is not in the Member DTO. Each flush then rebuilds members(): O(members × online) find, a sort that allocates lowercase strings per comparison, and a JSON encode for dedup. It also rebuilds server_summary() (one unread query per visible channel) and refresh_dms() (per DM: a message query, unread, get_contact, and a peer_online scan). Dedup suppresses only the emit, not the work. Correction: this path does not mark channels, so the 'duplicated channel queries' part does not apply. The cost is a few ms per roster update per server, a small idle CPU waste rather than wrong behaviour.

confirmed.title: Image serving copies every blob twice, reads the whole blob for HEAD, and loads every image in the history eagerly
confirmed.scenario: file_for_url reads the whole blob (up to 25 MiB) into Bytes and then calls `bytes.to_vec()`, a second full copy (transfers.rs:371-381). The shell builds the response from that copy (protocol.rs:79). A HEAD request does the full read and copy only to send headers (protocol.rs:72, 78). The in ImagePreview has no loading="lazy" (Attachment.tsx:117), and every loaded message stays in the DOM. So opening or scrolling a page of 30 image messages starts 30 concurrent full reads at once. Transient peak is about 2 × the total size in the Rust process, for example 30 × 10 MB × 2 = 600 MB, on top of the renderer decoding every image, including the ones off screen.
confirmed.fix: Return Vec::from(bytes) instead of bytes.to_vec(); it reuses the buffer when the Bytes is uniquely owned and Vec-backed. Add loading="lazy" and decoding="async" to the preview , with a sized placeholder: the .image-preview box needs a fixed or min size before load, or lazy loading has no effect. Optionally answer HEAD from files.status(hash) without reading the body.
confirmed.verify: Partly confirmed. file_for_url reads the whole blob into Bytes and then copies it with to_vec() (transfers.rs:371-381), so each image request briefly holds 2× its size, up to 25 MB each, before the response hands it to WebView2. ImagePreview's (Attachment.tsx:117) has no loading="lazy", and every loaded message stays mounted, so every complete image in the loaded pages is read and decoded eagerly. The HEAD part is moot in practice: loads issue GET, not HEAD. Transient memory only, no growth.

confirmed.title: The attachment index holds every attachment ever seen, then is wiped all at once, which breaks downloads of attachments already shown
confirmed.scenario: index_attachments runs for every message the app sees, the whole history sync included, even for attachments that are never fetched or shown (pump.rs:232, transfers.rs:258, views.rs:335-347). Each AttRef holds two 32-byte ids, a name of up to 255 chars and a MIME string, about 150-400 B. When the map passes 50,000 entries (about 10-20 MB, next to a measured idle private set of 9-11 MB) it is cleared entirely. Entries that existed only in memory are lost; they are persisted only when a download is requested or a file is sent (transfers.rs:175, 233). After the wipe, clicking Download on an attachment already on screen fails with 'This file isn't available on this device.' (transfers.rs:352), and queued Auto items are silently skipped (transfers.rs:103). Growth: one entry per attachment across every joined server's history.
confirmed.fix: Replace the clear-all with bounded eviction of the oldest entries: an insertion-order VecDeque, or an LRU touched by att_ref and message_dto, evicting the oldest past the cap. A smaller cap (for example 10k) is fine because page loads re-index. Optionally, on an att_ref miss in cmd_download, search the conversation's stored messages before failing.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed but an edge case. index_attachments runs for every message seen, history sync included (pump.rs:232, transfers.rs:258, views.rs:335-347). Past 50,000 entries (app.rs:30) the map is cleared entirely. Entries are persisted only on start_download or send (transfers.rs:175, 233). After a wipe, Download on a card rendered before it fails with 'This file isn't available on this device.' (transfers.rs:352), until a page reload or a message event re-indexes it (message_dto, views.rs:311). Queued Auto, Peers and Requery items whose entries were wiped are skipped silently (transfers.rs:103, 108, 121). Reaching 50k needs that many distinct attachments seen in one session, since after a restart the index refills only from page loads. That is very large for this app's scale.

confirmed.title: screen_unwatch can overtake an in-flight screen_watch, leaving a sink that streams frames to a dead channel until the share ends
confirmed.scenario: ScreenPlayer.start sends invoke('screen_watch') (ScreenView.tsx:45). If the view unmounts while that call is in flight, stop() closes the JS channel, which only swaps onmessage for a no-op (client.ts:122-125), and sends screen_unwatch through the separate `api` command (61). The two are independent async Tauri commands on a multi-thread runtime, so their order is not guaranteed. If unwatch runs first, watch then inserts the sink (screen.rs:303-321). That sink returns true for every frame, because Channel::send still succeeds and only page reloads stop it (commands.rs:29-31). The host keeps forwarding and Rust keeps copying and sending every frame at the share frame rate (30-60 per second) until the share ends or I leave voice.
confirmed.fix: In ScreenPlayer, keep the screen_watch promise. In stop(), call screen_unwatch only after it settles: `(this.watching ?? Promise.resolve()).finally(() => invoke('screen_unwatch', ...))`. Alternatively, have the shell's sink check a per-watch cancelled flag that screen_unwatch sets.
confirmed.verify: A genuine ordering race, but rare. ScreenPlayer.start sends screen_watch (ScreenView.tsx:45). stop() closes the JS channel, which only replaces onmessage, and sends screen_unwatch through the separate api command (61). These are independent async Tauri commands spawned onto a multi-thread runtime, with nothing serializing them. If unwatch runs first, watch() (screen.rs:303-321) then inserts a sink that keeps returning true: Channel::send succeeds and only a page reload stops it (src-tauri commands.rs:29-31). The host then forwards and Rust copies frames until the share ends or I leave voice (prune_watchers). Hitting it needs a full unmount, such as switching the stage tile or navigating away, inside one IPC round trip after the watch was sent, with the runtime running the later command first. A remount on the same track is harmless, because the new watch replaces the old sink.

confirmed.title: "Leave voice" during an outgoing ring only cancels the ring: the UI drops voice, but the room session and the mic stay live
confirmed.scenario: 1. Join the Lounge voice room. 2. Open a DM and press Call. While it rings, `s.voice` is the room and `s.call` is ringing-out. 3. CallPanel shows the room panel, because the "Calling" row at CallPanel.tsx:26 needs `!voice`. Its only red button is "Leave voice". 4. Press it. leaveVoice takes the `s.voice?.kind === "call" || s.call` branch: it calls `call_hangup` and then `patch({ voice: null, call: null })`. 5. Backend: `Media::call_hangup` (session.rs:668) calls `net.call_hangup`. `end_call` (tincan-net hub.rs:702) ends only the call and leaves `st.room` alone. `reconcile` sees the room attachment as still current, and `emit_voice` (session.rs:369) skips the event because the payload equals `last_voice`. No `voice-updated` corrects the UI. Result: the call panel disappears and the user thinks they left, but the engine keeps sending their microphone to everyone in Lounge. They still appear in the room for others and in their own sidebar (from members). While in a room there is also no control to cancel the outgoing ring.
confirmed.fix: In actions.ts leaveVoice, branch on `s.voice?.kind`. For "room", invoke `voice_leave` (Net::voice_leave only hangs up an Active call, hub.rs:452-463, so a ring in either direction survives), then `patch({ voice: null, soundboardOpen: false, fullStage: false })` and keep `call`. For "call", or no voice with a non-null call, invoke `call_hangup` and clear both. Add `cancelCall()`: invoke `call_hangup`, then `patch({ call: null })`. In CallPanel.tsx, render the "Calling <name>" row with its Cancel button (wired to cancelCall) whenever `call?.state === "ringing-out"`, including above the room panel when `voice?.kind === "room"`.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed end to end. ChatView.tsx:51 and MemberList.tsx:50 only count a call or a call-kind voice as busy, so a user in a room can press Call. hub.rs:525-567 call_start keeps `st.room`. CallPanel.tsx:26 hides the Calling row whenever `voice` is set, so the room panel's "Leave voice" button (CallPanel.tsx:61) is the only red control. leaveVoice (actions.ts:647) sees `s.call` and invokes call_hangup. Media::call_hangup (session.rs:668-673) calls Net::call_hangup (api.rs:77), then hangup (hub.rs:618), then end_call (hub.rs:702-715), which removes only `st.call`. State::active (hub.rs:85-90) returns the room whenever the call is not Active, so voice_info() still names the room. The reconcile stale check (session.rs:225-228) keeps the room attached, and emit_voice (session.rs:369) dedupes. No voice-updated event corrects the UI's `voice: null` patch (actions.ts:648), the engine stays attached and the mic keeps sending to the room. The same path declines an incoming call (RingingIn) instead of leaving the room when the user is in a room and presses Leave voice. The panel self-heals only when the room DTO next changes (someone joins, leaves or mutes, actions.ts:386); in a quiet room the hidden hot mic lasts until then. Re-clicking the room recovers it through voice_join's early return (session.rs:570).

confirmed.title: DM-only contacts look offline and can't be called once the DM link has idled out (120 s) or after a restart
confirmed.scenario: Alice adds Bob by Tincan ID; they share no server. They exchange messages, then wait over 120 s, or Alice restarts. Bob stays online the whole time. tincan-net closes idle DM connections after 120 s (notes-tincan-net.md:69, dm.rs:478). `DmSummary.online` is `net.peer_online` (views.rs:358), which for a peer with no shared server is only `dm.is_connected`, so `dm-updated` flips Bob to offline. Opening the conversation from DmSidebar (`openDms`) does not call `open_dm`, so nothing dials. In DmChat the Call button is `disabled={!dm.online || busy}` and the tooltip says "Bob is offline", though `call_start` would dial Bob itself (hub.rs:537 `net.dm.connect`). Calling a DM contact from the DM view only works within two minutes of the last message. The header and the sidebar dot also show the wrong presence.
confirmed.fix: The fix that matters: drop `!dm.online` from the Call button's `disabled` (keep `busy`) and let call_start report "Couldn't reach them right now." (hub.rs:559, or the dial timeout) when the contact really is unreachable. Change the tooltip so it no longer claims they are offline, for example always `Call ${dm.name}`. Optionally, have DmChat invoke `open_dm` once on mount (Net::dm_open calls ensure_connect, net.rs:466) to refresh presence. That only helps for about 120 s, because the idle close flips `online` back while the chat stays open. The header "Online/Offline" label and the sidebar dot stay unreliable for DM-only contacts; consider hiding presence for them when no server is shared.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. dm_summary sets `online` from `net.peer_online` (views.rs:358). For a peer who shares no server, peer_online is only `dm.is_connected` (inner.rs:264-270). run_conn closes an idle DM link after dm_idle = 120 s (dm.rs:478-485, timing.rs:94) unless it is held or has pending events. DmLinkDown then marks a dm refresh (pump.rs:318-320), and dm-updated flips the contact to offline. At startup, peers_seen dials only contacts with pending events (net.rs:146, dm.rs:143-149), so after a restart DM-only contacts show offline. The DmChat Call button is `disabled={!dm.online || busy}` (ChatView.tsx:65), yet call_start would dial on its own through net.dm.connect (hub.rs:537). For a contact added by ID, the DM view is the only place to call from, so calling fails unless a message went through in the last 2 minutes. The workaround (send a message first) is not discoverable.

confirmed.title: Deleting a voice room leaves the people inside connected to a room nobody can see
confirmed.scenario: The owner deletes the voice room Lounge while Bob and Sam are talking in it. The confirm dialog says "The room is removed for everyone." `Change::Channels` only refreshes channel DTOs (pump.rs:252-255) and never tells media. `Media::reconcile`'s stale check (session.rs:225-228) only compares conv and channel id and ignores `deleted`. The SFU checks for a deleted channel only on VoiceJoin (sfu.rs:445). Bob and Sam keep their session, their call panel still says "Lounge / <server>" (voice_dto reads `all_channels`, which includes deleted channels), and the mic stays live. The room row is gone from every sidebar (`view.channels` drops deleted channels), so nobody else can see who is still talking. At the next host migration their re-sent VoiceJoin is silently refused.
confirmed.fix: In the Change::Channels arm of pump.rs, after invalidate_view, call a new sync `core.media.on_channels(&core, conv)`. Under the st lock it checks `matches!(a.kind, Kind::Room { server, channel } if server == conv)` and `core.view(&conv).and_then(|v| v.all_channels.get(&channel).map(|c| c.deleted)) == Some(true)`. If so, it spawns a task (the pump is sync, and Media::voice_leave awaits the `ops` lock) that runs `core.media.voice_leave(&core).await` and toasts "The voice room was deleted.". voice_leave already reconciles and emits voice-updated null. Keep the change inside tincan-app.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. The Change::Channels arm (pump.rs:252-255) only invalidates the view and refreshes channels; Media is not told. on_net_event (media/mod.rs:362-389) ignores ConvUpdated. The reconcile stale check (session.rs:225-228) compares only conv and channel, and Net's voice_info still reports the room because nothing in hub.rs ends a room when its channel is deleted. The deleted check exists only at join time (hub.rs:415, sfu.rs:445/631). voice_dto reads the name from `all_channels`, which includes deleted channels (views.rs:51, session.rs:426). The sidebar uses `view.channels`, the visible list (views.rs:49). So the people inside keep talking in a room no one else can see or join, despite the "removed for everyone" text (ServerDialogs.tsx:333). After a host migration their re-sent VoiceJoin is dropped (sfu.rs:445-448). They can still leave by hand, so the impact is small.

confirmed.title: A call started from the member list never shows the call stage, so the peer's screen share and per-user volume can't be reached
confirmed.scenario: In a server text channel, Alice opens Bob's member menu and picks Call. `startCall` only patches `call`. When Bob accepts, Alice's view stays on the server channel. The call stage (VoiceStage), the only place a call peer's screen share and the tile context menu for per-user volume are rendered, exists only inside DmChat (ChatView.tsx:71). Bob presses Share screen; Alice sees nothing and gets no hint that he is sharing (CallPanel has no sharing indicator). She has to go to Direct messages and find the conversation herself. The callee, by contrast, is navigated to the DM in acceptCall (actions.ts:701).
confirmed.fix: Navigate the caller to the conversation. Simplest: in actions.ts startCall, `run(invoke("open_dm", { userId }).then((dm) => { update((s) => ({ ...s, dms: upsert(s.dms, dm, (x) => x.convId === dm.convId) })); openDms(dm.convId); return invoke("call_start", { userId }); }).then((call) => patch({ call })))`. Alternatively, open the DM when `call-updated` reports the caller's call as active. Making the CallPanel label a button that opens the DM for `voice.kind === "call"` would also cover a caller who navigated away.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. The member menu's Call calls `startCall(m.userId)` (MemberList.tsx:17), and startCall only patches `call` (actions.ts:690-692). VoiceStage, the only place a call peer's screen share and the per-user volume context menu are rendered, is mounted only in DmChat when `inCall` (ChatView.tsx:50,71-75) and in VoiceRoomView for rooms. CallPanel has no link to the conversation and no sharing indicator. The callee is navigated in acceptCall (actions.ts:701-702); the caller from a server channel is not. Low, because the DM does exist (call_start opens it, hub.rs:535) and "Call with <name>" appears in the panel, so the user can find it by hand.

confirmed.title: The per-user volume slider always starts at 100%, ignoring the volume the backend saved
confirmed.scenario: Alice sets Sam to 30%. `set_user_volume` saves it in kv `app/user_volumes` (session.rs:720) and re-applies it in every later session (session.rs:312, `apply_volumes`). After a restart Alice right-clicks Sam's tile: the slider reads `volumes.get(p.userId) ?? 1`, a module-level map that starts empty, so it shows 100% while Sam actually plays at 30%. Nudging the slider then sends about 100% and wipes the saved value. The contract has no way to read the saved volume: VoiceParticipant has no volume field, and there is no command for it.
confirmed.fix: Add `volume: number` (0..2) to VoiceParticipant in types.ts and dto.rs. Set it in voice_dto (session.rs:388-444) to `st.volumes.get(&user).copied().unwrap_or(1.0)` for others and 1.0 for me. Seed VolumePopover with `useState(() => p.volume)` and drop the module map. Also update every VoiceParticipant literal: the synthesized self entry (VoiceView.tsx:127-134), the non-joined room tiles (VoiceView.tsx:246), and the mock's participant builders (mock.ts). Because voice_dto now includes the volume, emit_voice after set_user_volume so the popover reopens with the new value.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. set_user_volume persists to kv `app/user_volumes` (session.rs:709-724), load_volumes reloads it at start (session.rs:148, media/mod.rs:251), and apply_volumes re-applies it in each session (session.rs:317-323). VolumePopover seeds from the module-level `volumes` map (VoiceView.tsx:14,17), which is empty after every app start, and VoiceParticipant (types.ts:122-130) carries no volume. After a restart the slider shows 100% while the user actually plays at the saved gain. The slider then saves whatever it is moved to, so the wrong part is the display before interaction.

confirmed.title: The Add sound picker offers .opus files, which the decoder can never read
confirmed.scenario: `CLIP_EXTENSIONS` includes "opus". tincan-audio decodes clips with symphonia 0.6, which has the mp3, aac, isomp4 and default features. Cargo.lock has no Opus codec crate, so `make_audio_decoder` fails ("unsupported codec", clip.rs:76). A user who picks a .opus file from the filtered dialog always gets "X isn't a sound Tincan can play. Pick an MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC or M4A file." (clips.rs:255).
confirmed.fix: Remove "opus" from CLIP_EXTENSIONS in Soundboard.tsx so the filter matches the formats named in the backend error. (Adding an Opus decoder through the existing unsafe-libopus codec would be a larger change in tincan-audio.)
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. CLIP_EXTENSIONS includes "opus" (Soundboard.tsx:14), and the file filter uses it (Soundboard.tsx:106). decode_clip uses only `symphonia::default::get_codecs()` (tincan-audio clip.rs:72-74). symphonia is built with features ["mp3","aac","isomp4"] (tincan-audio/Cargo.toml:14), and Cargo.lock has no opus codec crate (only vorbis, flac, mp3, aac, pcm, adpcm). An Ogg Opus file demuxes but fails make_audio_decoder with "unsupported codec", so clip_add always returns "... isn't a sound Tincan can play. Pick an MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC or M4A file." (clips.rs:254-256). The picker offers a format that can never work.

confirmed.title: Settings > Network says "No peers" for a server this PC hosts, even with members connected
confirmed.scenario: Alice hosts a server with 4 members online. tincan-net reports `path: None` for the Hosting state (session/host.rs:206), so `ServerSummary.connection.path` is "none". NetworkTab renders `path ? ... : "No peers"`, so the connection status reads "Hosted by you" next to "No peers" while 4 peers are connected.
confirmed.fix: In NetworkTab, branch on `c.state`. For "hosting", show `${Math.max(0, s.onlineCount - 1)} connected` (or "Hosting") in the neutral class. Keep the path or "No peers" text for member, solo, connecting and offline.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. HostRole::info returns `path: PathKind::None` for Hosting (tincan-net session/host.rs:202-209). server_summary passes it through as `path_kind(info.path)` (views.rs:249). NetworkTab renders `path ? ... : "No peers"` (SettingsDialog.tsx:365-371), so a host with connected members reads "Hosted by you" (hostLine, ChannelSidebar.tsx:21-22) next to "No peers". notes-tincan-app.md:258 acknowledges that hosting has no path, and voice_dto works around it (session.rs:382-387), but this tab does not.

confirmed.title: Sending a DM doesn't update lastMessageAt, so the DM list (newest first) doesn't move that conversation up
confirmed.scenario: Alice has DMs with Bob and Cara and sends Cara a message while the DM link is up. The pump emits `message-added` but marks the conversation dirty only when `event.event.author != core.me` (pump.rs:228-230). No `dm-updated` carries the new `lastMessageAt`, and the UI's sendMessage doesn't patch `dms` either. DmSidebar sorts by `lastMessageAt` (DmSidebar.tsx:13), and `openDms()` uses it to pick the most recent conversation (actions.ts:441), so Cara's conversation stays below older ones. A DM-only profile with no roster refreshes keeps the wrong order until the peer replies.
confirmed.fix: In pump.rs Change::Message, mark own messages too: `self.mark(conv, if event.event.author != core.me { Refresh::UNREAD } else { Refresh { dm: true, ..Refresh::default() } })`. The flush dedupes unchanged DTOs (emit_if_changed), and for server convs `dm: true` is ignored.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. For my own messages the pump emits message-added but does not mark the conversation (pump.rs:227-230). cmd_send_message (commands.rs:219-243) emits nothing else, and sendMessage only calls putMessage (actions.ts:574-577, 187-211), which does not touch `dms`. markSeen skips my own messages (actions.ts:251), so no mark_read refresh follows. on_dm_delivered emits only message-updated (commands.rs:304-323). So lastMessageAt goes stale, and DmSidebar's newest-first sort (DmSidebar.tsx:13) and openDms' recent pick (actions.ts:441-444) are wrong. It is self-corrected by refresh_dms on roster changes (pump.rs:269-272) or by DmLinkUp, so it mostly shows in DM-only or quiet profiles.

confirmed.title: The auto-fetch dropdown offers 50 and 100 MB, but the backend silently clamps them to 25 MB
confirmed.scenario: In Settings > Files the user picks "Up to 100 MB". `settings_set` clamps `autoFetchLimit` to `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` (settings.rs:65). saveSettings then patches the returned value, and the select jumps back to "Up to 25 MB" with no message. The 50 and 100 MB choices can never be saved; attachments are capped at 25 MB anyway.
confirmed.fix: Set `FETCH_LIMITS = [0, 5 * MB, 10 * MB, 25 * MB]` in SettingsDialog.tsx. The existing "include current value" branch (lines 270-272) still covers any odd stored value.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. FETCH_LIMITS offers 50 and 100 MB (SettingsDialog.tsx:266, MB = 1024², line 20). settings::normalize clamps autoFetchLimit to MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 25 MiB (settings.rs:11,65). saveSettings patches the returned value (actions.ts:779-780), so the select snaps back to "Up to 25 MB" with no message. The two larger choices can never be saved, and they would be meaningless because attachments cannot exceed 25 MiB.

rejected.title: settings_set read-modify-apply is not atomic; concurrent calls diverge memory, DB and live state
rejected.reason: Concurrent invocation is possible, but the race window cannot be hit in practice. cmd_settings_set is fully synchronous. Its window between reading `old` and writing self.settings is one SQLite save under WAL with synchronous=NORMAL (tincan-store lib.rs:92-99), behind the storage mutex: sub-millisecond to a few ms. The only caller is SettingsDialog user input: switch clicks, selects, and sliders debounced by 250 ms (SettingsDialog.tsx:198-202). Two settings_set calls cannot arrive within that window from human input, and nothing calls it programmatically.

rejected.title: Capability grants far more than the UI uses (core:default pulls in image-from-path, tray, menu and path, plus unused window setters)
rejected.reason: The over-grant itself is factual: core:default expands to the image, menu, path, tray and webview defaults (gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json). The concrete outcomes the finding claims do not happen. src-tauri/Cargo.toml uses `tauri = { features = [] }`, and the compiled fingerprints in target/a-shell show tauri built with only common-controls-v6, compression, dbus, default, dynamic-acl, wry and x11. Without image-png or image-ico, plugin:image|from_path is the stub that returns Err('from_path is only supported if the image-ico or image-png Cargo features are enabled') (tauri image/plugin.rs:51-55). The tray plugin is not registered at all without the tray-icon feature (app.rs:1268). What is left (menu creation, path resolution, window close or minimize) gives a script nothing beyond what the always-allowed app commands already give. window_close exists, and send_message accepts arbitrary absolute attachment paths (transfers.rs:428-453), which already lets any in-window script read files up to 25 MB and send them to a peer. No injection path is shown either, since the CSP is script-src 'self'. This is least-privilege hygiene, not a defect with a path.

rejected.title: Profile validation accepts Windows reserved device names (nul, and con/aux/prn/comN/lptN on Windows 10)
rejected.reason: This holds only for `nul` on this machine. In a scratch test on Windows 11 26200, GetFullPathNameW mapped ...\profiles\nul to \\.\nul and makedirs failed. con, aux, com1 and lpt1 normalised to ordinary paths and were created fine, so the Windows 10 half of the claim is unverified here. The only input path is a local user deliberately typing `--profile nul` or setting TINCAN_PROFILE=nul. The profile switch is a developer and e2e feature, and nobody hits that by accident. The outcome is that Tincan still refuses to start, just with a less precise message: the WebView2 or disk-writable text instead of INVALID_NAME. Nothing is written to a device and no data is touched. The 'con:' test case does not show reserved names were meant to be rejected, because the colon already fails the charset. The proposed snippet also does not compile, since `upper` is never bound.

rejected.title: The reserved device-name check misses COM¹-³, LPT¹-³ and names with a space before the dot
rejected.reason: The claimed outcome does not hold up. cmd_open_file always exports to an absolute path: download_dir must be absolute (settings.rs normalize), and the export goes to dir.join(name). On this machine (Windows 11 build 26200) I called RtlIsDosDeviceName_U and GetFullPathNameW. With a directory prefix, "COM1", "CON", "COM¹", "CON .txt", "NUL .txt" and "NUL.txt" are all NOT device names. Only bare "NUL" is, and safe_file_name already prefixes it. Even a bare "COM¹" maps to \\.\COM¹, not \\.\COM1, and there is normally no COM¹ symlink. So "writes the attachment bytes to the COM1 serial port" is not supported on any Windows version. I did not test Windows 10. There the worst realistic result is that the export of the attacker's own oddly named file fails with "Couldn't save the file to the download folder". The peer could get the same result by sending a broken file, so there is no meaningful security or functional impact.

rejected.title: File events are starved behind net events and a lag is only logged, so completed attachments are never announced and stale parked entries stay
rejected.reason: The starvation mechanism does not hold up. The biased select prefers net_rx, but file_rx is polled whenever net_rx is momentarily empty. In bulk, the pump's per-event work is µs-scale: rate counter, bulk bookkeeping, and an auto_fetch that returns early or does a try_send. Net ingest is bounded by signature checks and SQLite writes and arrives in page bursts, so net_rx is empty on most iterations. A possible stall path is the single Mutex<Connection> in tincan-store (lib.rs:52), shared by net writes and the pump. But on_transfer touches SQLite only on a state change (`changed && Attachment`); progress events are in-memory only. File events arrive at tens per second at most (3 active downloads × 4 progress events per second plus state changes), so a 512-event backlog would need about 20 s with the pump never seeing an empty net_rx. No such path was found. The missing resync on Lagged (pump.rs:121) is a latent hardening gap, not a reachable defect.

rejected.title: MessageList is not memoized, so typing, server, channel and voice updates reconcile every loaded row
rejected.reason: The facts are right but the impact is a nit. MessageList is not memo-wrapped, and ChannelChat and DmChat re-render on typing, server, channel and voice updates (ChatView.tsx:18, 48-52). But rows are memoized on `list` (MessageList.tsx:148), and each MessageItem is React.memo with unchanged prop references, so a parent re-render costs n element creations plus n shallow compares, all bailing out. That is sub-millisecond at normal list sizes. The layout effect depends on rows, firstKey and lastKey, so it does not re-run. It only matters when n is huge, which is RESOURCES-5's issue, not a separate defect.

rejected.title: The picker never shows "no hardware encoder" in place of the grid: screen_sources never returns that error
rejected.reason: The facts are true, but this is not a defect against the contract. types.ts:265 documents `no-hardware-encoder` as an error of `screen_start`. notes-ui.md:19 and the mock (mock.ts:1333) also raise it only from screen_start, and the backend matches that (screen.rs:191-193). The picker still reaches the no-encoder screen in place of the grid after Share (ScreenPickerDialog.tsx share() → setPhase no-encoder), exactly as in the reference mock flow. The cost is one extra click on rare hardware; the screen_sources handler in ScreenPickerDialog.tsx is defensive dead code, not a broken path.

rejected.title: No host-migration notice: the real backend never says who took over, though the mock does
rejected.reason: No spec requires a migration notice. design.md:62 only asks for the "Hosted by <name>" header line "(real state from the session)". The backend provides it: ConnectionChanged marks a server refresh (pump.rs:274-279), and server_summary carries host_id and host_name (views.rs:246-249). The mock's toast comes from a console dev helper (`migrate()`, mock.ts:1505-1512, notes-ui.md:19), not a contract item. Treating it as a requirement would be a feature request.
